heading: Short title
review_reason: Short title of the Abandoned Property Law; changes no rule's reach.

heading: Declaration of policy
review_reason: Declaration of policy for the Abandoned Property Law; it states no operative rule.

heading: Definitions
review_reason: Definitions of banking organizations, utility services, gift certificates and similar terms; none governs the ABP 1315 deposit-refund rules the settlement relies on.

heading: Unclaimed surplus from sale of pledged property
review_reason: Surplus from sales of pledged property by licensed pawn lenders; not a deposit refund.

heading: Unclaimed surplus from sale of pledge
review_reason: Surplus from a pledgee's sale of pledged goods; a landlord holds no pledge and may not hold belongings for rent (NY:COMMONLAW-belongings-owner-keeps).

heading: Unclaimed personal property of persons in certain state institutions
review_reason: Property of persons discharged from state institutions; not a tenancy.

heading: Unclaimed surplus moneys after recovery of cost of public assistance and care
review_reason: Surplus held by public welfare officials after recovery of assistance costs; not a landlord holder.

heading: Abandoned property resulting from the administration of the vehicle and traffic law
review_reason: Abandoned property held by the motor vehicle and tax commissioners; not held by a landlord or manager.

heading: Unclaimed proceeds from the sale of wrecked property
review_reason: Unclaimed proceeds from sales of wrecked property held by sheriffs and county treasurers; outside the chain.

heading: Unclaimed wages
review_reason: Unclaimed wages held by the Department of Labor; outside the chain.

heading: Uncashed travelers checks and money orders
review_reason: Uncashed travelers checks and money orders held by their issuers; a landlord's uncashed refund check is reported under ABP 1315 (NY:ABP-1315(2)).

heading: Voluntary disposition of miscellaneous property not otherwise subject to this chapter
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Unclaimed moneys erroneously collected by utility corporations on account of taxes
review_reason: Taxes erroneously collected by utility corporations; not a landlord holder.

heading: Unclaimed amounts or securities held by foreign corporations not authorized to do business in the state of New York
review_reason: The 1315 refund-reporting rule is stated; 1312 extends it to an owner entity chartered elsewhere and not authorized in New York when the tenant's last known address is in New York, without publication.

heading: Unclaimed property held by sales finance companies and insurance premium finance agencies
review_reason: Refunds held by sales finance companies and premium finance agencies; not a landlord holder.

heading: Unclaimed consumer credit balances
review_reason: Consumer credit balances transferable under GBL 715; a lease is not consumer credit (NY:ADJ-lease-balance-not-consumer-credit), so the deposit refund is reported under ABP 1315.

heading: Miscellaneous unclaimed property
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Unclaimed insurance proceeds other than life insurance
review_reason: Unclaimed non-life insurance proceeds held by insurers; not a landlord holder.

heading: Unclaimed security deposits held by the title insurance companies
review_reason: Security deposits held by title insurers in real property transfers; not a tenant deposit.

heading: Unclaimed spousal and child support
review_reason: Support payments held by support collection units; not a landlord holder.

heading: Unclaimed virtual currency
review_reason: Unclaimed virtual currency held by virtual-currency businesses; not a landlord holder.

heading: Statutes of limitations not a bar
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Comptroller to maintain public record
review_reason: The Comptroller's public record of abandoned property; no landlord act turns on it.

heading: Publication of abandoned property by state comptroller
review_reason: The Comptroller's online publication of abandoned property; no landlord act turns on it.

heading: Sale of personal property by state comptroller
review_reason: The Comptroller's sale of abandoned property after delivery; nothing the landlord or tenant does in the settlement turns on it.

heading: Assumption of liability by the state
review_reason: No rule states that paying the unclaimed refund to the Comptroller discharges the landlord; 1404 does, and bars suits against the holder for the property or later interest.

heading: Accrual of interest after payment of abandoned property to the state comptroller
review_reason: Once an unclaimed refund is paid to the Comptroller, the former tenant earns no further interest on it; this closes the deposit-interest account at the payment date.

heading: Claims for abandoned property heretofore or hereafter paid to the state
review_reason: How an owner claims abandoned property from the Comptroller; after reporting, the landlord is discharged (proposed NY:ABP-1404-holder-discharged) and the tenant's claim runs against the State.

heading: Payment by comptroller
review_reason: Payment of allowed claims by the Comptroller; no landlord act turns on it.

heading: Payment for publication
review_reason: Charges holder publication costs against abandoned property; a 1315 deposit refund carries no holder publication duty, so nothing is deducted under it.

heading: Designation of newspapers
review_reason: Newspapers for notices the chapter requires; a 1315 refund carries no holder publication.

heading: Waiver of publication
review_reason: The Comptroller's power to waive publication; no landlord or tenant act turns on it.

heading: Penalty, interest and special proceedings 1
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Retention of books and records
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Penalty for fraudulent returns
review_reason: The landlord's unclaimed-refund report is made under oath; a wilful false oath in it is perjury.

heading: Comptroller to make regulations
review_reason: The Comptroller's rulemaking power; the holder reporting guidance relied on is stated (NY:OSC-MS11-refunds-due).

heading: Deduction of certain charges
review_reason: No rule bars the holder from taking service, handling or dormancy charges out of an unclaimed refund; 1415 does, save deductions under New York law or a specific contract term made in the normal course.

heading: Restriction on agreement to locate and/or retrieve abandoned property
review_reason: Regulates fee-charging locators who help owners retrieve property already held by the Comptroller; no landlord, manager or Handoff settlement act turns on it.

heading: Agreements with other states
review_reason: The Comptroller's reciprocal agreements with other states; no landlord act turns on it.

heading: Property for New York residents held by other states
review_reason: The Comptroller's recovery of New York residents' property held by other states; no landlord act turns on it.

heading: Reporting of abandoned property in the aggregate
review_reason: Changes what the landlord's unclaimed-refund report must contain for refunds of $20 or less.

heading: Property held by agricultural cooperative corporations
review_reason: Exempts property held by agricultural cooperatives from the Abandoned Property Law; no landlord is such a cooperative.

heading: Property held by rural electric cooperatives
review_reason: Exempts property held by rural electric cooperatives; outside the chain.

heading: Mailing of notice to owners of record
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Authorization of foreign corporations
review_reason: The capacity bar on a foreign corporate owner is stated with 'doing business' left as a judgment; 1301(b) removes from that judgment the acts of suing, settling claims and keeping bank accounts, and 1301(d) takes a fictitious name filed with the corporation's authority out of the GBL 130 assumed-name precondition.

heading: Application to existing authorized foreign corporations
review_reason: Keeps in force authority issued under statutes before the BCL; a corporation's current authority is what the stated BCL 1312 rule checks.

heading: Violations
review_reason: Attorney General's action to restrain or annul a foreign corporation's authority; enforcement by the State, not a step for the owner, manager or tenant in the settlement.

heading: Application for authority
review_reason: Contents of a foreign corporation's application for authority; the filing the stated capacity rule requires, with no condition on the tenancy or the suit.

heading: Application for authority
review_reason: Authority begins on the Department of State's filing of the application and lasts while not surrendered, suspended or annulled; the stated rule's pre-suit check is exactly whether that authority is in force.

heading: Powers of authorized foreign corporations
review_reason: Powers of an authorized foreign corporation match a domestic one's; leasing and suing are within them, so nothing in the chain turns on it.

heading: Tenure of real property
review_reason: A foreign corporation may hold and convey New York real property; ownership of the building is a fact the chain starts from, and the transfer rules on sale are stated (GOL 7-105).

heading: Amendments or changes
review_reason: Matters a foreign corporation may amend in its application; the consequence of a missed amendment is decided under BCL 1309.

heading: Certificate of amendment
review_reason: The capacity bar is stated; 1309(c) adds that a foreign corporation that changed its name or state of incorporation and did not file an amendment within 20 days has its authority suspended, which again bars its suit until an amendment is filed.

heading: Certificate of change
review_reason: Certificate of change of a foreign corporation's office, process address or registered agent; a filing with no effect on its authority or on the tenancy.

heading: Surrender of authority
review_reason: Surrender of a foreign corporation's authority and service on the Secretary of State afterward; after surrender a suit on a pre-surrender lease is only the maintaining of an action, which BCL 1301(b)(1) excludes from doing business (proposed at NY:BCL-1301-doing-business-and-fictitious-name), so the section adds nothing further.

heading: Termination of existence
review_reason: Filing of a foreign corporation's termination and continued service on the Secretary of State; service of the tenant's process, not a settlement step.

heading: Actions or special proceedings by unauthorized foreign corporations
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Actions or special proceedings by foreign corporations
review_reason: A foreign corporation sues like a domestic one except as statute prescribes; the statutory bar that matters (authority to do business) is the stated rule.

heading: Actions or special proceedings against foreign corporations
review_reason: Lists when non-residents may sue a foreign corporation in New York; a former tenant's claim on an NYC lease qualifies under (b)(1)-(3), so nothing in the landlord's decisions changes.

heading: Record of shareholders
review_reason: Resident shareholders' inspection of a foreign corporation's shareholder records; internal corporate governance.

heading: Voting trust records
review_reason: Voting-trust records of foreign corporations; internal corporate governance.

heading: Liabilities of directors and officers of foreign corporations
review_reason: Liability of a foreign corporation's directors and officers under BCL 719-720 to the corporation; it gives a tenant no claim against the owner's officers and changes no settlement step.

heading: Liability of foreign corporations for failure to disclose required information
review_reason: Disclosure to resident shareholders of dividends and share changes; internal corporate governance.

heading: Applicability of other provisions
reason: APPLICABILITY: applicability or scope section in a unit that has a stated rule
review_reason: Lists shareholder and governance provisions applied to foreign corporations; internal governance.

heading: Exemption from certain provisions
review_reason: Exempts listed or mostly out-of-state foreign corporations from BCL 1316(e), 1317(a)(1), 1318 and 1319(a)(4); governance provisions outside the chain.

heading: Short title
review_reason: Short title and general application of the CPLR; the specific CPLR rules carry the steps.

heading: Amendment, rescission or adoption of rules
review_reason: Only the Legislature amends CPLR rules and no amendment changes substantive rights; no party step.

heading: Form of civil judicial proceedings
review_reason: One form of civil action, and actions versus special proceedings; no settlement step turns on it.

heading: Construction
review_reason: Liberal construction of the CPLR; a canon that adds no step or amount.

heading: Definitions
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Civil and criminal prosecutions not merged
review_reason: A civil claim is not merged in a criminal prosecution for the same act; the landlord's damage claim survives any prosecution without any step by the landlord.

heading: Appendix of official forms
review_reason: Chief Administrator's appendix of official CPLR forms; the forms a landlord must use (the commercial-claims demand letter) are fixed by the stated CCA rules.

heading: Application of article
review_reason: The limitation rules state the periods; 201 adds that a shorter period may be set by written agreement and that no court may extend a limitation period. A lease clause shortening the tenant's time to sue over the deposit is void under GOL 7-108's anti-waiver clause.

heading: Cause of action accruing without the state
review_reason: The borrowing statute: where a claim over the tenancy accrues outside New York in favor of a non-resident (an owner entity based out of state, a tenant who moved away before its claim accrued), the shorter of New York's and that place's period applies. Can bar the landlord's balance suit or the tenant's deposit suit early.

heading: Method of computing periods of limitation generally
reason: UNIVERSE: cited by an independent review universe item (U106, U5A-080)
review_reason: Fixes when a limitation period starts and stops (accrual to interposition) for the landlord's balance suit and the tenant's deposit suit, and saves a time-barred counterclaim from the same lease as a setoff; no rule states this.

heading: Stay of commencement of action
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Termination of action
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Termination of certain actions related to real property
review_reason: Recommencement rules only for actions on instruments under CPLR 213(4) (mortgages and other real-property secured instruments); a lease balance or deposit claim is not one (its recommencement is CPLR 205(a), stated).

heading: Computing periods of limitation in particular actions
review_reason: Where a lease makes a sum payable only on the landlord's demand, the period runs from when the landlord could first demand, not from the demand; a deposit held as trust money is not a 'special demand' deposit. Fixes accrual of such charges.

heading: Defendant's absence from state or residence under false name
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Infancy, insanity
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: In custody at time of cause of action
review_reason: Extra two-year window for injury claims of persons in correctional custody; no deposit or balance claim is such an injury claim.

heading: War
review_reason: Tolls limitation periods while a party cannot sue because of a war between the United States and the country where it resides or of which it is a national; applies to a former tenant or owner in such a country.

heading: Death of claimant or person liable
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Actions to be commenced within twenty years
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Actions to be commenced within ten or fifteen years
review_reason: Ten- and fifteen-year periods for recovering real property, annulled patents and mortgage redemption; none is a claim in the settlement chain.

heading: Actions to be commenced within six years: where not otherwise provided for
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Residential rent overcharge
review_reason: Residential rent overcharge claims arise only for rent-stabilized or rent-controlled units (regulated rent); out of aperture for a market-rate unit (Review 2).

heading: Action by a victim of a criminal offense
review_reason: A crime victim may sue the convicted defendant within seven years of the crime; a landlord whose unit was damaged or property stolen by a former tenant convicted of that crime has seven years, longer than the six-year contract period.

heading: Action by victim of conduct constituting certain sexual offenses
review_reason: Limitation periods for civil claims arising from sexual offenses; not a claim in the settlement chain.

heading: Actions to be commenced within three years
review_reason: Three-year limit on medical debt actions by hospitals and health professionals; not a lease balance.

heading: Actions to be commenced within three years: for non-payment of money collected on execution
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Action for medical, dental or podiatric malpractice to be commenced within two years and six months
review_reason: Limitation period for medical, dental and podiatric malpractice; the lease and deposit limitation periods are stated.

heading: Action to recover damages for personal injury caused by contact with or exposure to phenoxy herbicides
review_reason: Limitation period for Agent Orange injury claims; outside the chain.

heading: Certain actions to be commenced within three years of discovery
review_reason: Discovery accrual for injury from latent exposure to substances (toxic torts); no claim in the settlement chain is of that kind.

heading: Limitations on certain actions against licensed engineers and architects
review_reason: Notice-of-claim and limitation rule for injury or property-damage claims against licensed architects and engineers over conduct more than ten years old; no claim between landlord and tenant.

heading: Action to recover damages for personal injury caused by the infusion of such blood products which result in the contraction of the human ...
review_reason: Revival of HIV blood-product injury claims; outside the chain.

heading: Action to recover damages for personal injury caused by contact with or exposure to any substance or combination of substances found with...
review_reason: Personal injury from superfund-site exposure; not a claim in the settlement chain.

heading: Certain child sexual abuse cases
review_reason: Revival window for child sexual abuse claims; outside the chain.

heading: Certain actions by public water suppliers to recover damages for injury to property
review_reason: Limitation period for public water suppliers' contamination claims; outside the chain.

heading: Certain actions arising out of consumer credit transactions to be commenced within three years
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Action to recover damages for personal injury caused by contact with or exposure to toxic burn pits
review_reason: Limitation period for burn-pit exposure injury claims of service members; outside the chain (the 214-i governing consumer credit is stated separately).

heading: Certain sexual offense actions
review_reason: Revival window for certain sexual-offense claims; not a claim in the settlement chain.

heading: Actions to be commenced within one year: against sheriff, coroner or constable
review_reason: 215(7) sets a one-year limit on a tenant's RPL 223-b(3) retaliation action, which the retaliation rule does not state; the other subdivisions (sheriff liability, assault, penalty to informer, arbitration award, interest overcharge) decide nothing in this chain.

heading: Abbreviation of period to one year after notice
review_reason: Where one person sues for a contract sum and another claims the same sum but cannot be served, the defendant may notify the other claimant and cut its time to sue to one year; a tool for a landlord facing competing claims to a deposit refund.

heading: Proceeding against body or officer
review_reason: Four-month limit for proceedings against bodies or officers (article 78) and union fair-representation claims; review of agency determinations is not a step in settling a market-rate tenancy.

heading: Actions to be commenced within one year and ninety days
review_reason: Notice of claim and a one-year-ninety-day limit for actions against public entities; no party to a market-rate tenancy settlement is one.

heading: Transitional provisions
review_reason: Transitional rules for claims that accrued before CPLR article 2 took effect in 1963; no current claim is affected.

heading: Jurisdiction over persons, property or status
review_reason: Preserves general personal jurisdiction as it existed before the CPLR (domiciliaries, entities at home here); reaching a former tenant who moved away is decided at proposed NY:CPLR-302-long-arm and NY:CCA-404-long-arm.

heading: Personal jurisdiction by acts of non-domiciliaries
review_reason: New York courts have personal jurisdiction over a non-domiciliary on a claim arising from its owning, using or possessing real property in New York, or transacting business here; a former tenant who moved out of state can be sued in New York for the balance, and an out-of-state owner for the deposit.

heading: Designation of attorney as agent for service
review_reason: A party beyond New York's jurisdiction who sues here (a moved-away tenant suing for the deposit) designates its attorney, or the clerk, as agent to be served in the landlord's separate action on a claim that could have been a counterclaim; changes how the landlord can reach that tenant.

heading: Method of commencing action or special proceeding
review_reason: In Supreme Court an action is commenced by filing the summons and complaint (or summons with notice) with the county clerk and paying the index fee; the filing date is the interposition date for limitations.

heading: Summons
review_reason: A Supreme Court summons must state the basis of venue (and the plaintiff's address if venue rests on its residence), the index number and filing date; a summons served without the complaint must state the nature of the claim, relief and the default amount. Changes what the landlord serves to commence.

heading: Proof of service
review_reason: Sets what the proof of service must show (papers, person, date, time, address, manner, a physical description of the person served, and the prior attempts for nail-and-mail); a defective affidavit exposes a default judgment to vacatur.

heading: Index number in an action or proceeding commenced in supreme or county court
review_reason: Assignment of the index number and payment of its fee on filing in Supreme or County Court; the fee's amount is CPLR 8018 and commencement is at proposed NY:CPLR-304-commencement.

heading: Service of the summons and complaint, summons with notice, or petition with a notice of petition or order to show cause
review_reason: In Supreme Court the summons must be served within 120 days after filing or the action is dismissed without prejudice unless extended; a deadline whose miss can end a claim filed near the limitations date.

heading: Notice of commencement of action for personal injuries by recipient of medical assistance
review_reason: Notice to social services of personal injury actions by Medicaid recipients; not a claim in the chain.

heading: Additional mailing of notice in an action arising out of a consumer credit transaction
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Personal service upon the state
review_reason: Service on the State and state officers; not a party to the tenancy.

heading: Personal service upon a natural person
review_reason: The methods of serving a natural-person former tenant (personal delivery; delivery at its actual dwelling or business plus mailing; affix-and-mail after due diligence; court-directed); a former tenant's vacated unit is no longer its dwelling, so service there is void. Decides whether any judgment on the balance is valid.

heading: Personal service upon an infant, incompetent or conservatee
review_reason: How to serve a former tenant who is an infant, an adjudicated incompetent or a conservatee (the parent, guardian, committee or conservator, and the person too); service otherwise gives no jurisdiction.

heading: Personal service upon a partnership
review_reason: How a partnership owner (or partnership tenant) is served; a tenant suing a partnership landlord serves any partner or the managing agent at its office plus mailing.

heading: Personal service upon a limited partnership
review_reason: How a limited partnership owner (or tenant) is served: its managing or general agent or general partner in New York, an authorized agent, or a designated person; fixes how a tenant sues an LP owner.

heading: Personal service upon a corporation or governmental subdivision
review_reason: How a corporation is served (an officer, director, managing or general agent, or authorized agent, or the Secretary of State under BCL 306); fixes how a tenant sues a corporate owner and how the landlord sues a corporate tenant.

heading: Personal service on limited liability companies
review_reason: How a limited liability company is served (a member or manager in New York, an authorized or designated agent, or the Secretary of State under the LLC Law); the usual route for a tenant suing an LLC owner, and for the landlord suing a company tenant organized as an LLC.

heading: Personal service upon a court, board or commission
review_reason: Service on courts, boards and commissions; not parties to the tenancy.

heading: Personal service by mail
review_reason: Service by mail with acknowledgment: complete only when the tenant returns the signed acknowledgment (within 30 days), answer due 20 days later, and the tenant pays the cost of other service if it does not return it; decides whether the cheap mail route works.

heading: Service without the state giving personal jurisdiction
review_reason: A former tenant domiciled in New York or subject to its long-arm jurisdiction (CPLR 302, for a claim arising from its lease of NYC property) may be served outside the state in the same manner as within; decides whether a tenant who moved out of state can be sued in Supreme Court.

heading: Service without the state not giving personal jurisdiction in certain actions
review_reason: Service outside the state without personal jurisdiction in matrimonial, in-rem and attachment-based cases; a personal balance or deposit claim is reached with personal jurisdiction under CPLR 302 (proposed NY:CPLR-302-long-arm).

heading: Service by publication authorized
review_reason: Publication is authorized only in the in-rem and status actions of CPLR 314, not a personal action for a lease balance; an unlocatable former tenant is served by a court-directed method under CPLR 308(5).

heading: Service by publication
review_reason: Form and timing of publication once ordered under CPLR 315; no publication route exists for a personal balance action (see CPLR 315), so it adds no step.

heading: Defense by person to whom summons not personally delivered
review_reason: A former tenant served other than by personal delivery who defaulted may reopen the judgment within one year after learning of it (at most five years after entry) if it did not receive the summons and has a meritorious defense, with restitution; a default judgment on substituted or nail-and-mail service stays open to this risk.

heading: Designation of agent for service
review_reason: Lets a person designate an agent for service by a filed, acknowledged writing; no settlement step turns on it (service on such an agent is a CPLR 308(3) method).

heading: Defendant's appearance
review_reason: In Supreme Court the former tenant must appear within 20 days after personal delivery, or 30 days after service is complete for substituted, affix-and-mail, out-of-state or publication service; fixes when a default arises.

heading: Attorneys
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Authority for appearance of attorney in real property action
review_reason: Proof of an attorney's authority in actions affecting real property; a balance or deposit action is not one.

heading: Grounds for removal
review_reason: Removal of actions between courts (mistake in court, limited jurisdiction, consent); a court power whose cost effect is CPLR 8104, adding no settlement step.

heading: Procedure on removal
review_reason: Procedure on removal; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Inconvenient forum
review_reason: A court's discretionary dismissal for inconvenient forum; a claim over an NYC tenancy is heard in New York, and the doctrine adds no step, amount or deadline for either side.

heading: Assistance to tribunals and litigants outside the state
review_reason: Service in New York for out-of-state tribunals; it does not bind recognition of foreign judgments and adds no step in the chain.

heading: Contractual provisions fixing venue
review_reason: A written venue clause agreed before suit (for example in the lease) is enforced on a motion to change venue; CPLR 514's ban on venue clauses in consumer-goods contracts does not reach a residential lease. Changes where the balance or deposit suit is tried.

heading: Conflicting venue provisions
review_reason: Resolving conflicting venue provisions on joinder; in-suit venue mechanics.

heading: Venue based on residence
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Actions against counties, cities, towns, villages, school districts and district corporations
review_reason: Venue of actions against municipalities; not parties to the tenancy.

heading: Actions involving public authorities
review_reason: Venue of actions involving public authorities; not parties to the tenancy.

heading: Where special proceeding commenced
review_reason: Where special proceedings (including article 78) are brought; article 52 enforcement proceedings follow CPLR 5221 (proposed NY:CPLR-5221-enforcement-forum).

heading: Real property actions
review_reason: Venue of actions affecting title to or possession of real property; a balance or deposit action is a money action.

heading: Actions to recover a chattel
review_reason: Venue of actions to recover a chattel; not a claim in the chain (belongings rules are stated).

heading: Venue in county designated
review_reason: The plaintiff's designated county governs until changed; the venue choice itself is decided by CPLR 503 and the proposed venue rules, and this adds no step.

heading: Grounds for change of place of trial
review_reason: Grounds on which a court may change venue (improper county, impartiality, convenience); the timing that binds a defendant is CPLR 511 (proposed NY:CPLR-511-venue-demand).

heading: Change of place of trial
review_reason: In Supreme Court a former tenant who objects to the landlord's county must serve a written demand with or before its answer and move within 15 days; otherwise venue stands. Mirrors the Civil Court rule.

heading: Change of place of trial of action or issue triable without a jury
review_reason: Place of trial for non-jury issues within the judicial district; in-suit mechanics.

heading: Misplacement of venue in consumer credit transactions
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Actions relating to consumer goods
review_reason: Voids venue clauses only in contracts for the sale or lease of consumer goods (goods, wares, merchandise or services); a residential lease of real property is not one, so the lease venue clause is governed by CPLR 501 (proposed NY:CPLR-501-venue-clause).

heading: Venue in matrimonial actions
review_reason: Venue in matrimonial actions; outside the chain.

heading: Necessary joinder of parties
review_reason: The court's standard for compelling joinder of absent parties; who may be sued alone on a joint lease obligation is CPLR 1501-1502, and who is paid a joint refund is NY:ADJ-cotenants-payee. It adds no step to the settlement.

heading: Permissive joinder of parties
review_reason: Permits joining co-tenants, occupants and guarantors as defendants in one action; who is liable is decided by the lease and NY:GOL-5-701(a)(2)-guaranty, and joinder adds no step or amount.

heading: Nonjoinder and misjoinder of parties
review_reason: Nonjoinder and misjoinder of parties and adding parties; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: When joinder unnecessary
review_reason: An executor, guardian or trustee may sue or be sued without joining beneficiaries; who is paid or sued after a tenant's death is stated at NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee.

heading: Interpleader
review_reason: A landlord facing conflicting claims to a deposit refund (co-tenants, an estate and a relative, a trustee and the tenant) may interplead the claimants, pay the refund into court and be discharged, owing interest only at the Federal Reserve discount rate absent agreement; decides how it pays safely.

heading: When third-party practice allowed
review_reason: Third-party practice (for example a sued tenant impleading a roommate); in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Answer of third-party defendant
review_reason: Answer of a third-party defendant; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Claim by plaintiff against third-party defendant
review_reason: Plaintiff's claim against a third-party defendant; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Dismissal or separate trial of third-party complaint
review_reason: Dismissal or separate trial of a third-party complaint; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Successive third-party proceedings
review_reason: Successive third-party proceedings; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Intervention as of right
review_reason: Intervention as of right (for example a co-tenant joining a deposit suit); in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Intervention by permission
review_reason: Permissive intervention; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

review_reason: Proposed pleading on intervention; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Substitution upon death

review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Substitution of committee or conservator
review_reason: The court substitutes a committee or conservator for a party adjudicated incompetent; a court act, with representation stated at the proposed NY:CPLR-1201-representation.

heading: Substitution in case of receivership or dissolution of a corporation
review_reason: The court substitutes proper parties when a party gets a receiver or a corporate party dissolves; a court act that adds no step for the settlement (who collects under a receiver is stated at NY:CPLR-6401-foreclosure-receiver).

heading: Substitution upon transfer of interest
review_reason: A pending action continues after a transfer of interest unless the court substitutes the transferee; who owns a pre-sale balance is decided by NY:RPL-223 and assignment limits by NY:JUD-489-champerty.

heading: Substitution of public officers
review_reason: Substitution of public officers; no public officer is a party to a market-rate tenancy settlement.

heading: Substitution of indemnitors for executing or attaching officer
review_reason: Substitution of an indemnitor for a sheriff sued over a levied chattel; officer litigation outside the chain.

heading: Substitution procedure
review_reason: The parties rule states substitution on death; 1021 adds that substitution must be sought within a reasonable time or the action may be dismissed (not on the merits), and that on a party's death the court orders the estate's interested persons to show cause.

heading: Substitution: extension of time for taking procedural steps
review_reason: Extends in-suit procedural deadlines until 15 days after substitution; litigation mechanics that change no step, amount or precondition of the settlement.

heading: Public body or officer described by official title
review_reason: Public bodies sued by official title; not parties to the tenancy.

heading: Unknown parties
review_reason: Suing a party whose name is unknown under a partial description; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Partnerships and unincorporated associations
review_reason: Partnerships sue and are sued in the firm name; it adds no step (partnership service is at proposed NY:CPLR-310-partnership).

heading: Review of determinations by administrative officers of the unified court system
review_reason: Names the Chief Administrator as the party when court administrative determinations are reviewed; outside the chain.

heading: Representation of infant, incompetent person, or conservatee
reason: UNIVERSE: cited by an independent review universe item (U5A-091)
review_reason: The parties rule bars a default against an infant or adjudicated incompetent; 1201 adds who appears for them and that an adult incapable of defending its rights appears by a guardian ad litem, which the landlord must obtain before pursuing an incapacitated former tenant.

heading: Appointment of guardian ad litem
review_reason: The parties rule bars a default against an infant or incompetent until a guardian ad litem is appointed; 1202 adds that the landlord, as another party, may move for the appointment if no relative or representative moves within ten days after service, with notice to the representative or household and the proposed guardian's consent.

heading: Default judgment
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Compensation of guardian ad litem
review_reason: A guardian ad litem appointed for an incapacitated or infant former tenant may be paid reasonable compensation by any other party, including the landlord that sued; a cost of pursuing such a tenant.

heading: Liability for costs of infant, judicially declared incompetent, or conservatee, or representative
review_reason: An infant, incompetent, conservatee or guardian-ad-litem-represented former tenant (or its representative) is not liable for costs unless the court orders; changes the landlord's recoverable costs against such a tenant.

heading: Disposition of proceeds of claim of infant, judicially declared incompetent or conservatee
review_reason: Money an infant, adjudicated incompetent or conservatee former tenant recovers (for example a deposit settlement or judgment) is paid to its guardian, committee or conservator, or as the court orders, not to the person; decides to whom the landlord pays.

heading: Settlement of action or claim by infant, judicially declared incompetent or conservatee, by whom motion made
review_reason: A settlement of a claim by an infant, adjudicated incompetent or conservatee (for example a deposit claim of a tenant under guardianship) binds only when the court approves it on the representative's motion or petition; decides whether a settlement with such a tenant is final.

heading: Settlement procedure
review_reason: The proposed CPLR 1207 rule makes a settlement with an infant or incapacitated former tenant bind only on court approval; 1208 fixes what the application must contain, who must attend, who may represent the tenant, and that the landlord's attorney may prepare the papers when the tenant has none. No rule states it.

heading: Arbitration of controversy involving infant, judicially declared incompetent or conservatee
review_reason: A controversy involving an infant or incapacitated person goes to arbitration only by court order; no arbitration route is part of this chain (the small-claims arbitration rule already excludes such parties).

heading: Guardian of infant
review_reason: Appointment of a guardian of an infant's property by petition; the landlord pays and settles through a guardian already appointed (proposed NY:CPLR-1206-proceeds-payee) and takes no step here.

heading: Allowance for infant's support
review_reason: Petition to apply an infant's property to its support; no landlord or tenant settlement step.

heading: Actions against persons jointly liable
review_reason: On a joint lease obligation the landlord may proceed against the co-tenants it has served and take judgment against all named; changes how a balance owed by co-tenants (one unreachable) is pursued.

heading: Provisional remedies and defenses in subsequent action against co-obligor
review_reason: To reach an unserved co-tenant's own property after a joint judgment, the landlord must bring a second, verified action, in which the co-tenant keeps all its defenses; decides whether pursuing an absent co-tenant is worth it.

heading: Mistakes, omissions, defects and irregularities
review_reason: Lets the court correct or disregard filing mistakes in a pending case; in-suit discretion that changes no step, amount or deadline of the settlement.

heading: Error in ruling of court
review_reason: Harmless-error rule for court rulings; appellate and trial review, no settlement step.

heading: Irregularity in judicial sale
review_reason: Lets the court set aside a judicial sale within a year for defective notice or manner; it binds the enforcement officer's sale and changes no step or amount in the landlord's settlement or collection decision.

heading: Extensions of time generally
review_reason: General judicial power to extend times set by statute or rule, except where the law expressly bars it (limitations periods cannot be extended: CPLR 201); it fixes no step or deadline of its own.

heading: Excusable delay or default
review_reason: Allows a court to excuse law-office failure on a motion to vacate a default; court discretion inside CPLR 5015 and 3012(d), adding no step or deadline.

heading: Form of papers
review_reason: Form, language, caption and signing of court papers; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Filing of papers
review_reason: Where papers are filed and that clerks accept them; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Service of papers
review_reason: How papers are served between parties after an action is begun (on the attorney, by mail with five added days, fax, overnight, electronic); in-suit mechanics that change no settlement step. Commencement service is CPLR 308-312-a and CCA 403.

heading: Confidentiality of addresses in civil proceedings
review_reason: A court may let a party keep its address confidential for safety, and the address of a domestic-violence program resident is never revealed; changes how a landlord serves and pursues a former tenant who is a domestic-violence victim.

heading: Stipulations
review_reason: A settlement with a former tenant in a pending case binds only if in a writing signed by the party or its attorney, made in open court, or so-ordered, and its terms are filed by the defendant with the county clerk; decides whether a settlement is enforceable.

heading: Certification by attorney
review_reason: Attorneys may certify copies; clerical, no settlement step.

heading: Affirmation of truth of statement
review_reason: Any person may sign a statement affirmed under penalty of perjury in the statutory form instead of a notarized affidavit; the manager's or Handoff's affidavits of facts, service or non-military status may be affirmations.

heading: Stay
review_reason: General power of a court to stay a pending action; the effect of a stay on limitations is stated at NY:CPLR-204-208-tolling and bankruptcy and military stays elsewhere. It adds no step.

heading: Application for order
review_reason: Defines a motion; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Where motion made, in supreme court action
review_reason: Where Supreme Court motions are heard; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Where motion made, in county court action
review_reason: Where County Court motions are heard; outside New York City.

heading: Motion papers
review_reason: Motion papers and service times; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Relief demanded by other than moving party
review_reason: Cross-motions; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Prior motion
review_reason: Prior motions, ex parte affidavits and transfer of motions; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Trial of issue raised on motion
review_reason: Trial of an issue raised on a motion; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Time and form of order
review_reason: Time and form of orders; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Entry and filing of order
review_reason: Entry, filing and service of orders; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Motion affecting prior order
review_reason: Motions to renew or reargue; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Docketing order as judgment
review_reason: On request the clerk dockets an order directing payment of money (including motion costs, a so-ordered payment) as a judgment, making it enforceable and interest-bearing; a step for enforcing a court-ordered payment from a former tenant.

heading: Duties of officer receiving mandate
review_reason: An enforcement officer's duties on receiving a mandate (receipt, copy, return); officer mechanics.

heading: Declaratory judgment
review_reason: Supreme Court declaratory judgments; no declaratory claim is a step in settling the account.

heading: Actions and relief not barred for inconsistency
review_reason: Suing one co-tenant or the guarantor, or holding an unsatisfied judgment against one, does not bar an action against the others; and a tenant may sue either the managing agent or the undisclosed owner. Changes whom the balance or deposit claim may be pursued against.

heading: Action for periodic payments due under pension or retirement contract no bar to action for future installments
review_reason: Suing for past pension installments does not bar later suits for future ones; limited to pension and retirement agreements, so it does not reach installments of rent.

heading: Where restoration of benefits before judgment unnecessary
review_reason: Rescission of a transaction void or voidable for fraud, mistake, duress or incapacity without tendering back benefits first; rescinding a lease is not a step in settling the account of a tenancy that has ended.

heading: Relief against mistake of law
review_reason: Removes the fact/law distinction when a court grants relief for mistake; whether a sum a tenant paid is refundable or credited is decided by the charge rules themselves (for example NY:RPL-238-a(1)-no-move-in-fees, NY:ADJ-no-fee-retention), so it adds no step to the account.

heading: Kinds of pleadings
review_reason: Kinds of pleadings; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Certificate of merit in medical, dental and podiatric malpractice actions
review_reason: Certificate of merit in medical malpractice actions; outside the chain.

heading: Certificate of merit in certain residential foreclosure actions
review_reason: Certificate of merit in residential mortgage foreclosure of a home loan; not a landlord-tenant claim.

heading: Particularity of statements generally
review_reason: Pleadings must give notice of the transactions and elements; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Statements
review_reason: Pleadings in numbered paragraphs; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Particularity as to specific matters

heading: Particularity in specific actions
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Demand for relief
review_reason: Pleading form for the demand for relief; the limit of a default judgment to the amount demanded is CPLR 3215(b). It adds no step in the chain.

heading: Responsive pleadings
review_reason: Defenses such as the statute of limitations, payment, release, bankruptcy discharge and res judicata must be pleaded or are lost; changes what the landlord (defending a deposit suit) or the tenant (defending a balance suit) must raise.

heading: Counterclaims and cross-claims
review_reason: A defendant may counterclaim any claim against the plaintiff, and counterclaims are permissive; where a collector or other nominal plaintiff sues on the owner's balance, the tenant's deposit claim against the owner is allowed as a counterclaim up to the plaintiff's claim.

heading: Verification
review_reason: Says who may verify the landlord's pleading: the owner, an officer of a domestic corporation, or an agent (managing agent) where the owner is a foreign entity or out of county or the facts are within the agent's personal knowledge; decides whether the manager can sign the verification.

heading: Form of affidavit of verification
review_reason: Wording of an affidavit of verification; who may verify is at proposed NY:CPLR-3020-verification. in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Remedy for defective verification
review_reason: Treats a defectively verified pleading as unverified and lets the opponent reject it on prompt notice; in-suit pleading mechanics with no settlement consequence.

heading: Construction of verified pleading
review_reason: How verified allegations are construed; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Motion to correct pleadings
review_reason: Motions to correct vague or scandalous pleadings; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Amended and supplemental pleadings
review_reason: Amending pleadings in a pending action; in-suit mechanics (relation back of an amended claim for limitations is stated at CPLR 203(f)).

heading: Construction
review_reason: Pleadings are construed liberally; a canon for the court that adds no step or amount.

heading: Simplified procedure for court determination of disputes--action without pleadings
review_reason: Voluntary simplified procedure by a statement signed by all parties; a litigation-format option that changes no amount, deadline or precondition.

heading: Contents of statement
review_reason: Contents of a simplified-procedure statement; a voluntary litigation format.

heading: Contracts to submit
review_reason: Enforces written contracts to use the simplified procedure; it concerns the forum format of a dispute both sides agreed to and changes no amount, deadline or precondition of the settlement.

heading: Motion procedure to settle statement terms
review_reason: Motion to settle a simplified-procedure statement under a contract to submit; a voluntary litigation format.

heading: Simplified procedure authorized
review_reason: Authorizes the simplified procedure's rules; a voluntary litigation format.

heading: Court determination
review_reason: How the court runs a simplified-procedure case (evidence rules relaxed, experts, default for failure to serve a statement); in-suit mechanics of a voluntary format.

heading: Appeal
review_reason: Appeals in simplified-procedure cases; appellate practice.

heading: Bill of particulars in any case
review_reason: A party may demand a bill of particulars or a copy of the items of an account in a pending suit; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Procedure for bill of particulars
review_reason: Procedure and preclusion for bills of particulars; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Bill of particulars in personal injury actions
review_reason: Bill of particulars in personal-injury actions; no deposit or balance suit is one.

heading: Verification of bill of particulars
review_reason: Verification of bills of particulars; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Arbitration of damages in medical, dental or podiatric malpractice actions
review_reason: Arbitration of damages in malpractice actions; outside the chain.

heading: Confession of judgment before default on certain installment contracts invalid
review_reason: Voids pre-default confessions of judgment only for installment purchases of consumer commodities of $1,500 or less; a lease balance is not such a purchase (confession for a lease balance is CPLR 3218).

heading: Motion to dismiss
review_reason: Lists the grounds on which the former tenant (or the landlord, when sued) can have a claim dismissed early (limitations, release, payment, lack of capacity, no personal jurisdiction, failure to state a claim) and when each is waived; decides which defects end the balance suit.

heading: Motion for summary judgment
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Motion for summary judgment in lieu of complaint
review_reason: An action on an instrument for the payment of money only, or on a judgment, may start with a summary-judgment motion instead of a complaint; decides whether a former tenant's signed payment note or a judgment can be enforced this fast track (a lease itself cannot).

heading: Motions heard by judge supervising disclosure
review_reason: Motions before the disclosure judge and the disclosure stay on dispositive motions; in-suit litigation mechanics that change no amount, deadline, precondition or payee in settling the account or deciding to pursue it.

heading: Default judgment
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Want of prosecution
review_reason: A landlord that sues and then neglects the case for a year after joinder can be served a 90-day demand to file a note of issue, after which the action may be dismissed; a deadline that can end the balance suit.

heading: Voluntary discontinuance
review_reason: How a landlord (or tenant) discontinues its claim, and that a second discontinuance by notice is an adjudication on the merits; decides whether withdrawing a suit (for example after a settlement or to re-file) forfeits the claim.

heading: Judgment by confession
review_reason: A former tenant may confess judgment by affidavit for the balance, filed within three years only in the county where the tenant resided, with the consumer-rate statement where it applies; a payment-plan security option with strict limits.

heading: Tender
review_reason: A landlord sued on the lease (for example for the deposit) may deposit a sum with the clerk and tender it; if the tenant does not beat it, the tenant loses interest and costs from the tender and pays the landlord's costs. A cost-shifting settlement tool.

heading: Offer to liquidate damages conditionally
review_reason: A party sued on the lease may offer to fix damages at a stated sum if it loses on liability; a claimant that refuses and does no better pays the expense of trying damages from the offer.

heading: Offer to compromise
review_reason: An offer to allow judgment for a stated sum: if accepted within ten days judgment is entered; if refused and the claimant does no better, it loses costs from the offer and pays the offeror's costs. A cost-shifting settlement tool in a deposit or balance suit.

heading: Action on submitted facts
review_reason: Actions on an agreed submission of facts; a voluntary litigation format.

heading: Self-incrimination
review_reason: A witness cannot refuse to answer because the answer shows it owes a debt; the judgment debtor's duty to answer on examination is stated through CPLR 5223-5224, and this adds no step.

heading: Spouse
review_reason: Spousal privilege; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Attorney
review_reason: Attorney-client privilege; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Physician, dentist, podiatrist, chiropractor and nurse
review_reason: Physician-patient privilege; an evidentiary privilege with no settlement step.

heading: Confidential communication to clergy privileged
review_reason: Clergy privilege; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Eavesdropping evidence
review_reason: Excludes recordings obtained by criminal eavesdropping; a participant's own recording of a call with a former tenant is not eavesdropping under Penal Law 250.05, so no settlement step turns on it.

heading: Psychologist
review_reason: Psychologist privilege; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Social worker
review_reason: Social worker privilege; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Library records
review_reason: Library records privilege; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Rape crisis counselor or domestic violence advocate
review_reason: Rape crisis counselor and domestic violence advocate privilege; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it. (The domestic-violence termination and address rules are stated elsewhere.)

heading: Judicial notice of law
review_reason: Judicial notice of law; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Competency of interested witness or spouse
review_reason: Interested parties and spouses are competent witnesses; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Competency of person convicted of crime
review_reason: Convicted persons are competent witnesses; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Impeachment of witness by prior inconsistent statement
review_reason: Impeachment by prior inconsistent statement; an evidentiary privilege or competency rule applied at trial; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Form of expert opinion
review_reason: Form of expert opinion testimony; trial evidence, no settlement step.

heading: Proof of age of child
review_reason: A child may be exhibited to prove age; a tenant's minority is a fact the stated incapacity rules take as given, and this evidentiary device changes no step.

heading: Prior testimony in a civil action
review_reason: Use of prior trial testimony; trial evidence, no settlement step.

heading: Business records
review_reason: The landlord proves the balance and each charge through business records (ledger, move-in record, inspection reports, invoices, the itemized statement, electronic records) made in the regular course of business at or near the time; this sets how Handoff and the manager must make and keep the settlement file.

heading: Personal transaction or communication between witness and decedent or person with a mental illness
review_reason: The dead man's statute: after a former tenant dies, the landlord and its interested witnesses cannot testify against the estate about personal transactions or communications with the tenant; claims against the estate must be proved by documents and disinterested witnesses.

heading: Possession of opioid antagonists
review_reason: Bars possession of an opioid antagonist as evidence of illegal use in illegal-use eviction proceedings; an eviction ground, not a step in settling the account.

heading: Certificate or affidavit of public officer
review_reason: Public officers' filed certificates are prima facie evidence; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Lack of record
review_reason: A custodian's statement of no record is prima facie evidence; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Ancient filed maps, surveys and records affecting real property
review_reason: Ancient filed maps and records affecting real property; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Search by title insurance or abstract company
review_reason: Title company searches in place of official searches; not used in the chain.

heading: Conveyance of real property without the state
review_reason: Records of out-of-state conveyances are prima facie evidence; not a step in a tenancy settlement.

heading: Copies of statements under article nine of the uniform commercial code
review_reason: Copies of UCC article 9 filings; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Marriage certificate
review_reason: Marriage certificate as prima facie evidence of marriage; no settlement step turns on proving a marriage.

heading: Death or other status of missing person
review_reason: Federal missing-person and presumed-death findings are prima facie evidence; the tenant-death and military rules stated elsewhere govern the settlement, and this evidentiary rule adds no step.

heading: Weather conditions
review_reason: Weather bureau records; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Inspection certificate issued by United States department of agriculture
review_reason: USDA inspection certificates; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Certificate of population
review_reason: Census certificates; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Affidavit of service or posting notice by person unavailable at trial
review_reason: An absent server's affidavit is prima facie proof of service or posting at trial; an evidentiary convenience that adds no step or requirement to the settlement.

heading: Self-authentication of newspapers and periodicals of general circulation
review_reason: Self-authentication of newspapers; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Admissibility of graphic, numerical, symbolic or pictorial representations of medical or diagnostic tests
review_reason: Medical and diagnostic test images; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: An image, map, location, distance, calculation, or other information taken from a web mapping service, a global satellite imaging site, o...
review_reason: Web mapping and satellite images are admissible if dated; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Market reports
review_reason: Published stock and commodity market reports are admissible to prove market price; rent, repair costs and deposits are not priced on such markets.

heading: Prima facie proof of damages
review_reason: In any civil action an itemized, receipted repair bill of $2,000 or less, certified by the vendor and served with notice ten days before trial, is prima facie proof of the reasonable value and necessity of the repair; sets how the landlord proves a damage charge outside small claims.

heading: Proof of payment by joint tort-feasor
review_reason: Deduction of a joint tortfeasor's settlement (GOL 15-108) in injury cases; the release rules between co-obligors on a lease are stated at NY:GOL-15-104-105-cotenant-release.

heading: Standard of measurement used by surveyor
review_reason: Surveyors' measurement standards; not used in the chain.

heading: Proof of writing by comparison of handwriting
review_reason: Handwriting comparison; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Proof of writing subscribed by witness
review_reason: Proof of writings with subscribing witnesses; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Acknowledged, proved or certified writing
review_reason: An acknowledged writing is prima facie proof of execution; residential leases are not acknowledged and the lease is proved as a business record or by the parties, so no step turns on it.

heading: Reproductions of original
review_reason: A scanned or electronic copy the business made in its regular course is as admissible as the original, and an image stored by a process that records any change is admissible when its tamper-protection is shown; governs keeping the settlement file digitally and discarding paper.

heading: Authentication of official record of court or government office in the United States
review_reason: Authentication of official records by attested copy; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it. (Registration and certificate-of-occupancy records are proved this way, but the step is the substantive check, stated at NY:MDL-301(1) and NY:MDL-325(2).)

heading: Presumption of authenticity based on a party's production of material authored or otherwise created by the party
review_reason: Material a party produces in disclosure is presumed authentic against it; in-suit evidence mechanics.

heading: Proof of proceedings before justice of the peace
review_reason: Proof of justice-of-the-peace proceedings; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Proof of foreign records and documents
review_reason: Proof of foreign records; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Proof of facts or writing by methods other than those authorized in this article
review_reason: Other lawful methods of proof are preserved; adds nothing.

heading: Contracts in small print
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Admissibility of collateral source of payment
review_reason: In an action for injury to property, a loss replaced by a collateral source (such as the owner's property insurance) reduces the award, net of two years' premiums, except payments carrying a statutory right of reimbursement; changes what the landlord recovers from a former tenant for insured damage.

heading: Loss of earnings and impairment of earning ability in actions for medical, dental or podiatric malpractice
review_reason: Tax treatment of lost-earnings awards in malpractice actions; outside the chain.

heading: Compromise and offers to compromise
review_reason: Settlement offers and statements made in compromise negotiations over a disputed balance or deduction are not admissible to prove liability or amount; changes how Handoff or the manager can negotiate with a former tenant.

heading: Privileged communications
review_reason: Privileged communications keep their privilege when sent electronically; no settlement step turns on it.

heading: Admissibility of an opposing party's statement
review_reason: Statements by the landlord's authorized agent or employee (the managing agent, Handoff, a collector) on matters within the agency are admissible against the landlord; what Handoff or the manager writes to a former tenant about a charge binds the owner as evidence.

heading: Admissibility of evidence related to legally protected health activity
review_reason: Evidence of legally protected reproductive or gender-affirming health activity may not be used to show wrongdoing; no settlement step turns on it.

heading: New York voting and elections database
review_reason: Presumed validity of the state voting and elections database; an evidentiary rule for a kind of record or proceeding that does not arise in settling a market-rate tenancy; no settlement, collection or record-keeping step turns on it.

heading: Interest to verdict, report or decision
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Interest from verdict, report or decision to judgment
review_reason: The interest rules state pre-decision interest and the rate; 5002 adds interest on the whole award (including interest to decision) from the verdict or decision to entry of judgment, computed by the clerk.

heading: Interest upon judgment
review_reason: The 2% rule names post-judgment interest but no rule states that a money judgment bears interest from entry (or a docketed money order from docketing).

heading: Prompt payment following settlement
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Nondisclosure agreements
review_reason: Limits confidentiality terms that an employer may put in settlements of discrimination claims; it binds employers, not a landlord settling a tenancy account.

heading: Rate of interest
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Definition and content of judgment
reason: DEFINITIONS: definition section in a unit that has a stated rule
review_reason: Defines a judgment and its contents (and payment into court for incarcerated plaintiffs); no settlement or collection step turns on it.

heading: Judgment upon part of cause of action
review_reason: Judgment on part of a claim after severance; in-suit mechanics.

heading: Effect of judgment dismissing claim
review_reason: A dismissal after the plaintiff has closed its evidence is on the merits unless it says otherwise, so the landlord (or tenant) cannot sue again; an earlier dismissal is not. Decides whether a failed suit can be re-brought.

heading: Action upon judgment
reason: UNIVERSE: cited by an independent review universe item (U5A-100)
review_reason: An action on a New York money judgment is allowed only after ten years from docketing (to renew the lien, begun in the ninth year), after a default on non-personal service, or by leave; this governs renewing a judgment against a former tenant.

heading: Relief from judgment or order
review_reason: The grounds and deadlines on which a former tenant (or the landlord) can vacate a judgment: excusable default within one year after service with notice of entry, lack of jurisdiction at any time, fraud or misconduct, new evidence, and mass vacatur of improper defaults, with restitution. Decides how durable a default judgment on the balance is.

heading: Entry of judgment
review_reason: When a judgment is entered and how after a verdict or a party's death; clerical mechanics (substitution and death are stated at NY:CPLR-1203-1015-5208-parties).

heading: Judgment-roll
review_reason: Preparation and contents of the judgment-roll; clerk and attorney mechanics.

heading: Docketing of judgment
