review_reason: Docketing of a money judgment (and by transcript in other counties) with the debtor's last known address; a docketed judgment is the lien on the former tenant's real property and must mark unsummoned joint debtors.

heading: Validity and correction of judgment or order
review_reason: A person other than the judgment creditor who becomes entitled to enforce the judgment (an assignee such as a collector or debt buyer) must file its acknowledged instrument with the clerk before enforcing; changes the steps when the landlord assigns a judgment.

heading: Satisfaction-piece
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Payment of judgment in certain cases
review_reason: A landlord that owes a former tenant a judgment, and whose certified-mail payment to the tenant's last known address came back, may deposit a certified check with the clerk to stop execution charges; the route for paying an unlocatable tenant's judgment.

heading: Entry of satisfaction
review_reason: The satisfaction rule states the creditor's duty to file a satisfaction-piece; 5021 adds how a paying judgment debtor gets satisfaction entered when the creditor will not furnish one (court order or deposit), and the sheriff's return of a small-claims execution within 90 days.

heading: Enforcement of money judgment or order
review_reason: Says a money judgment or money order is enforced under CPLR article 52; the article 52 rules themselves carry the steps and limits (NY:CPLR-5205-5231-enforcement-limits and the article 52 rules proposed in this batch).

heading: Enforcement of judgment or order awarding possession of real property or a chattel
review_reason: Enforces a judgment awarding possession by execution; in this chain possession is back when the tenant leaves, and an NYC eviction is enforced by an RPAPL warrant, not a CPLR 5102 execution.

heading: Enforcement of judgment or order directing sale of real property
review_reason: Enforcement of judgments directing sale of specific real property (foreclosure, partition); not a money judgment on a lease.

heading: Enforcement of judgment or order by contempt
review_reason: Contempt enforcement of judgments not enforceable under article 52 or 5102; a money judgment on a lease balance or deposit is enforced under article 52 (the fiduciary exception is CPLR 5105).

heading: Alternative enforcement of judgment or order
review_reason: A judgment requiring a trustee or fiduciary to pay money for a willful default may be enforced by contempt as well as by execution; the landlord holds the deposit in trust (GOL 7-103), so a judgment for a deposit it willfully withheld or commingled carries contempt exposure.

heading: Appointment of receiver
review_reason: Receiver to carry out a judgment about specific property; not a money judgment on a lease (enforcement receivers are CPLR 5228, proposed).

heading: Conveyance by sheriff
review_reason: Court may direct the sheriff's conveyance; enforcement-officer or court mechanics that add no step, amount or deadline for the landlord or tenant.

heading: Debt or property subject to enforcement
review_reason: The enforcement-limits rule states the exemptions; 5201 states what the landlord can reach (any assignable debt or property, present or future, in or out of state) and that a joint-liability judgment reaches individual property only of co-tenants summoned.

heading: Judgment creditor's rights in personal property
review_reason: Priority between an execution creditor and third parties who acquire the debtor's property; it decides contests with transferees, not any step, amount or deadline in the landlord's settlement or collection.

heading: Priorities and liens upon real property
review_reason: A docketed money judgment is a lien on the former tenant's real property in that county for ten years (extendable for stays or a pending sale); decides what enforcement against a tenant who owns property yields.

heading: Release of lien or levy upon appeal
review_reason: Release of a judgment lien or levy when the debtor posts an appeal undertaking; appellate practice that changes no settlement or collection step.

heading: Personal property exempt from application to the satisfaction of money judgments
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Real property exempt from application to the satisfaction of money judgments
review_reason: The enforcement-limits rule covers bank and wage exemptions but not the homestead: a former tenant's owned and occupied home is exempt up to $150,000 of equity in NYC (adjusted under CPLR 5253), which caps recovery from real property.

heading: Enforcement involving the state
review_reason: The State as judgment debtor or garnishee; a former tenant's state wages are reached by the income execution already stated (NY:CPLR-5205-5231-enforcement-limits), adding no step.

heading: Enforcement after death of judgment debtor
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Discharge of garnishee's obligation
review_reason: When a creditor of the former tenant levies on or restrains the deposit refund the landlord owes the tenant, paying the sheriff or creditor under the execution or order discharges the landlord to that extent; decides who the refund is paid to.

heading: Power of court to punish for contempt
review_reason: Gives enforcement courts contempt power over enforcement procedures; it adds no step, amount or deadline for the landlord or tenant (the subpoena warning is in CPLR 5223).

heading: Privilege on examination
review_reason: Lets a court confer criminal-law immunity on a witness in an enforcement examination on notice to the district attorney; no settlement or collection decision turns on it.

heading: Where enforcement proceeding commenced
review_reason: An enforcement proceeding on an NYC Civil Court judgment against a tenant who lives or works in the city is brought in the Civil Court; otherwise in Supreme or County Court where the tenant lives or works. Decides where the landlord enforces.

heading: Restraining notice
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Service of notices and forms and procedure for claim of exemption
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Disclosure
review_reason: Until the judgment is satisfied, the landlord may compel disclosure of anything relevant to collecting it by a subpoena stating the parties, judgment and amount due, and warning of contempt; the tool for finding a former tenant's assets.

heading: Subpoena
review_reason: The enforcement subpoenas the landlord may serve (deposition, documents, information subpoena by certified mail with 7-day answers), the reasonable-belief certification without which a third-party information subpoena is void, and the one-year bar on re-examining the tenant.

heading: Payment or delivery of property of judgment debtor
review_reason: Turnover: the court orders the former tenant, or a third party holding the tenant's money or property, to pay or deliver it to satisfy the landlord's judgment; an enforcement route against a tenant with identifiable funds.

heading: Installment payment order
review_reason: The court may order a former tenant with income to pay the judgment in installments fixed with regard to its and its dependents' reasonable needs; the main route against a tenant with income but no leviable assets.

heading: Payment of debts owed to judgment debtor
review_reason: By special proceeding the court may order anyone who owes the former tenant money to pay it to the landlord up to the judgment, or enter judgment against that person; reaches the tenant's receivables.

heading: Receivers
review_reason: The court may appoint a receiver to collect or sell the former tenant's property to satisfy the judgment, at up to 5% commission (none if the landlord itself is receiver); an enforcement option with its cost.

heading: Enforcement before judgment entered
review_reason: After a decision in the landlord's favor and before judgment is entered, the trial judge may order the former tenant examined and restrained as if a post-judgment restraining notice had been served; stops dissipation of assets.

heading: Executions
review_reason: The enforcement-limits rule covers exemptions; no rule states the execution's required contents (the 2% consumer rate, last known address, exemption notices), who issues it, or its 60-day return.

heading: Income execution
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Levy upon personal property
review_reason: The enforcement-limits rule states the bank exemption; 5232 adds the levy's 90-day life, the 4-day notice to a natural-person debtor, the 27-day bank hold with exemption forms, and the creditor's liability for naming a third party's property.

heading: Sale of personal property
review_reason: How the sheriff conducts an execution sale of personal property (auction, notice, unsaleable goods); the officer's duties, not a step or amount for the landlord or tenant.

heading: Distribution of proceeds of personal property
review_reason: Proceeds of a levy go to the judgment creditor after fees, excess to the former tenant, not before 15 days after service; competing executions are paid in delivery order. Decides when and in what order the landlord is paid.

heading: Levy upon real property
review_reason: The sheriff's method of levying on real property after the ten-year docketing lien lapses (a filed notice of levy); officer mechanics. The landlord's real-property rights are stated at the proposed NY:CPLR-5203-real-property-lien and NY:CPLR-5014-renewal-judgment.

heading: Sale of real property
review_reason: The sheriff's procedure for an execution sale of real property (notice, publication, deed, distribution); a former tenant's residence is reached only through the homestead special proceeding (proposed NY:CPLR-5206-homestead), and the sale mechanics add no settlement step.

heading: Failure of title to property sold
review_reason: An execution-sale purchaser's recovery of the price if title fails; a remote contest after a sheriff's sale that adds no settlement step.

heading: Directions to the sheriff
review_reason: Court directions to the sheriff on levied property; enforcement-officer or court mechanics that add no step, amount or deadline for the landlord or tenant.

heading: Proceeding to determine adverse claims
review_reason: Anyone claiming an interest in levied property (a joint account holder, a spouse, the former tenant) may bring a proceeding to decide it, and the court may void the levy and award damages; changes the landlord's exposure when it levies property that is not only the tenant's.

heading: Modification or protective order
review_reason: General power of the court to limit or condition any enforcement procedure on request; judicial supervision that adds no step, amount or deadline of its own.

heading: Income execution for support enforcement
review_reason: Income executions for child and spousal support; a landlord's income execution on a money judgment is CPLR 5231, stated at NY:CPLR-5205-5231-enforcement-limits.

heading: Income deduction order for support enforcement
review_reason: Income deduction orders for child and spousal support; not a landlord's judgment.

heading: Arrest of judgment debtor
review_reason: A court may order the arrest of a judgment debtor about to leave the state or in hiding with property, to bring it in for examination; an extraordinary enforcement step against a departing former tenant.

heading: Disobedience of subpoena, restraining notice or order
review_reason: Disobeying an enforcement subpoena, restraining notice or order, or false swearing on an examination, is contempt; this binds a landlord served with a restraining notice on a former tenant's refund, and a tenant that ignores the landlord's subpoena.

heading: Discrimination against employees and prospective employees based upon wage assignment or income execution
review_reason: Bars employers from discriminating against employees over wage assignments or income executions; it binds the tenant's employer, not the landlord's settlement or collection.

heading: Cost of living adjustment for personal and real property exempt from application to the satisfaction of money judgments and exemptions in...
review_reason: The enforcement-limits rule states the exemptions at their statutory amounts; 5253 makes the CPLR 5205 and 5206 dollar exemptions adjust every three years from April 1, 2012 by the published CPI figure, not applying to restraints or executions made before an adjustment.

heading: Kinds of provisional remedies
review_reason: Lists the provisional remedies and requires disclosure of other remedies sought; the attachment rules proposed at CPLR 6201-6223 carry the steps.

heading: Grounds for attachment
review_reason: Grounds for a pre-judgment order of attachment against a former tenant: it lives outside New York, cannot be served despite diligence, or is hiding or moving assets to defeat a judgment; an option to secure the balance against a tenant who has left the state.

heading: Debt or property subject to attachment
review_reason: Defines attachable property by reference to CPLR 5201 (proposed NY:CPLR-5201-reachable-property); it adds nothing of its own.

heading: Attaching creditor's rights in personal property
review_reason: Priority of an attaching creditor over later transferees of the defendant's property; a contest with third parties, not a settlement or collection step.

heading: Discharge of garnishee's obligation
review_reason: When a creditor of the former tenant attaches the refund the landlord owes the tenant, paying the sheriff under the order of attachment discharges the landlord to that extent; decides who the refund is paid to.

heading: Order of attachment in certain cases
review_reason: Attachment in aid of a judgment against a foreign state; outside the chain.

heading: Order of attachment on notice
review_reason: Attachment on notice and an interim restraint on garnishees; mechanics within the proposed attachment rules (CPLR 6201, 6211, 6212).

heading: Order of attachment without notice
review_reason: An attachment granted without notice must be confirmed on motion within 5 days after levy (10 days for a nondomiciliary defendant), or it lapses; a deadline that decides whether the landlord keeps its security.

heading: Motion papers
review_reason: To attach, the landlord must show probable success and that its claim exceeds known counterclaims (for example the deposit), post an undertaking of at least $500, file within ten days, and is liable for all damages and attorney's fees if the attachment was wrongful; decides whether attaching is worth it.

heading: Service of summons
review_reason: An attachment granted before the former tenant is served is valid only if the summons is served (or publication begun and completed) within 60 days; a deadline on the landlord's security.

heading: Levy upon personal property by service of order
review_reason: How an attachment levy binds a garnishee: it must hold and turn over the defendant's property or debts for 90 days; binds a landlord holding a former tenant's refund when the tenant's creditor attaches, and sets the 90-day life of the landlord's own levy.

heading: Levy upon personal property by seizure
review_reason: Levy by the sheriff's physical seizure on the plaintiff's direction and indemnity; officer mechanics that add no settlement step beyond the attachment rules proposed at CPLR 6201-6214.

heading: Levy upon real property
review_reason: The sheriff levies an attachment on real property by filing a notice with the county clerk; officer mechanics.

heading: Additional undertaking to carrier garnishee
review_reason: Undertaking to a common-carrier garnishee; not a party in the chain.

heading: Sheriff's duties after levy
review_reason: The sheriff's custody of attached property in an interest-bearing trust account and inventory; officer duties, not the landlord's.

heading: Garnishee's statement
review_reason: A garnishee served with an order of attachment must within ten days serve the sheriff a statement of its debts to and property of the defendant; binds a landlord served by a former tenant's creditor while holding the tenant's refund.

heading: Disclosure
review_reason: Court-ordered disclosure about attached property; enforcement-officer or court mechanics that add no step, amount or deadline for the landlord or tenant.

heading: Proceedings to determine adverse claims
review_reason: Adverse claimants to attached property may have their rights decided; it mirrors CPLR 5239 (proposed NY:CPLR-5239-adverse-claims) for attachment, and the landlord's damages exposure for a wrongful attachment is stated at proposed NY:CPLR-6212-attachment-motion.

heading: Discharge of attachment
review_reason: Lets the defendant free attached property by posting an undertaking for its value; the tenant's option, adding no step for the landlord.

heading: Vacating or modifying attachment
review_reason: The former tenant, a garnishee or any interested person may move to vacate an attachment, and the landlord bears the burden of proving the grounds, the need for the levy and probable success; after the tenant appears the court vacates an attachment that is unnecessary for security.

heading: Annulment of attachment
review_reason: An attachment ends automatically when the action is discontinued, the judgment is satisfied, or the defendant wins; no step for the landlord.

heading: Return of property
review_reason: Directions to the clerk and sheriff to release attached property; enforcement-officer or court mechanics that add no step, amount or deadline for the landlord or tenant.

heading: Disposition of attached property after execution issued
review_reason: After execution issues, attached property is handled as if levied under the execution, with priority by delivery (CPLR 5234); officer mechanics.

heading: Appointment and powers of temporary receiver
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Oath
review_reason: Oath of a temporary receiver; the receiver's duty.

heading: Undertaking
review_reason: Undertaking of a temporary receiver; the receiver's duty.

heading: Accounts
review_reason: Temporary receivers' accounts; the receiver's duty, not the landlord's.

heading: Removal
review_reason: Court's power to remove a receiver it appointed; a receiver's right to rents is stated at NY:CPLR-6401-foreclosure-receiver, and removal adds no landlord step.

heading: Persons subpoenaed
review_reason: A non-party subpoenaed to testify or produce records gets $15 a day plus mileage outside a city (and $3 more at an examination before trial); a cost the landlord tenders when it subpoenas a bank or employer to find a former tenant's assets.

heading: Stenographers
review_reason: Stenographer's transcript fees by court rule; a litigation expense with no settlement step or recoverable-amount rule of its own.

heading: Referees
review_reason: Referees' fees; no referee is used in settling or collecting the account.

heading: Commissions of receivers
review_reason: Receivers' commissions (up to 5%); stated for enforcement receivers at proposed NY:CPLR-5228-receiver.

heading: Commissions of trustees
review_reason: Commissions of trustees of express trusts; internal to trusts.

heading: Premiums on undertakings by fiduciaries
review_reason: Fiduciaries' bond premiums as expenses; not the landlord's cost.

heading: Printers
review_reason: Newspaper publication rates; no publication route exists for a balance or deposit action (see CPLR 315).

heading: Fees and expenses of officer to be paid before transmission of paper
review_reason: Officers transmit papers only on request and payment of fees; enforcement-officer or court mechanics that add no step, amount or deadline for the landlord or tenant.

heading: Oaths
review_reason: Fees of officers for oaths and acknowledgments ($2); affirmations under CPLR 2106 avoid them, and they are not a decision in the chain.

heading: County treasurers
review_reason: The NYC Commissioner of Finance takes 2% of money paid out of court; a deposit refund the landlord pays into court (interpleader, or a tender left unclaimed) reaches the claimant less 2%, which the court may charge against the fund.

heading: Fixed fees of sheriffs
review_reason: Sets the sheriff's fixed fees for executions, income executions, attachments and service, largely payable in advance; an enforcement cost in the pursue-or-write-off estimate, recovered from the tenant through the execution.

heading: Mileage fees, poundage fees, additional compensation, and limitation on compensation of sheriffs
review_reason: The sheriff takes 5% poundage in NYC on sums collected, and on a settlement after levy is owed poundage on the lesser of the judgment or the settlement; a settlement with the former tenant after a levy carries this cost.

heading: Expenses of sheriffs
review_reason: The sheriff's reimbursable expenses (publication, appraisal, custody) and its right to advance payment; these are recovered through the execution under CPLR 8014 and add no step or amount decision of their own.

heading: Collection of sheriff's fees on execution
review_reason: Sheriff's fees on a property execution not in the creditor's bill of costs are collected from the judgment debtor under the execution; so they fall on the former tenant, not the landlord, when collection succeeds.

heading: County clerk where sheriff is a party or otherwise disqualified
review_reason: County clerk's fees when acting for a disqualified sheriff; enforcement-officer or court mechanics that add no step, amount or deadline for the landlord or tenant.

heading: Clerks of courts of record generally
review_reason: Fees of clerks of courts of record other than the NYC Civil Court and county clerks; not the courts where this chain's suits are brought.

heading: Exemption of the state and counties, and agencies and officers thereof, from fees of clerks
review_reason: Fee exemptions for the State and counties; not parties to the tenancy.

heading: Index number fees of county clerks
review_reason: Commencing a Supreme Court action costs a $190 index-number fee (plus $20 in surcharges), which covers later filings including judgment and satisfaction docketing; a cost of choosing Supreme Court for the balance suit.

heading: County clerks generally
review_reason: County clerks' general recording and copying fees; none is a step in a lease-balance or deposit suit beyond the index fee (CPLR 8018).

heading: County clerks as clerks of court
review_reason: Supreme Court fees after filing: $95 request for judicial intervention (needed for any motion, including a default judgment motion), $45 per motion, $30 to calendar, $65 jury demand, and $35 paid by the defendant to file a settlement or discontinuance; costs in the pursue decision and on settling a suit.

heading: County clerks other than as clerks of court
review_reason: County clerk fees outside court actions include $25 in New York City to file a transcript of a Civil Court judgment and $15 to issue a transcript of the docket; the cost of docketing the landlord's judgment to reach real property or other counties.

heading: Fee on civil appeals proceedings before appellate courts
review_reason: Fees on civil appeals; appellate practice.

heading: Costs in an action
review_reason: The party that wins judgment gets costs unless a statute says otherwise or the court finds it inequitable; decides whether costs are added to the landlord's balance judgment or the tenant's deposit judgment.

heading: Limitation of costs where action brought in higher court
review_reason: A landlord that sues in Supreme Court in NYC for what the Civil Court could hear gets no costs unless it recovers $6,000 or more; a cost consequence of forum choice.

heading: Costs where parties prevail upon separate issues
review_reason: Where the landlord recovers on the balance but the tenant prevails on a distinct claim (for example its deposit counterclaim), the court may award costs to both; changes the net costs in a mixed result.

heading: Costs in consolidated, severed or removed action
review_reason: Costs in consolidated, severed or removed actions; an allocation rule for unusual procedural postures that changes no settlement step.

heading: Costs where more than one plaintiff or defendant
review_reason: Several winning parties share one set of costs unless ordered otherwise; an allocation detail that changes no step or recoverable amount decision in the settlement.

heading: Costs upon motion
review_reason: Motion costs are discretionary; their amount is capped by CPLR 8202 (proposed) and in Civil Court by CCA 1906 (proposed). Adds nothing of its own.

heading: Costs upon appeal
review_reason: Costs on appeal; appellate practice.

heading: Specification of denial or award of costs
review_reason: Where a court's denial or award of costs must be stated; drafting mechanics for the court.

heading: Defendant's costs against the state
review_reason: Costs awarded to a defendant against the State; the State is not a party to the tenancy.

heading: Costs against a fiduciary
review_reason: Costs awarded against a fiduciary (a deceased tenant's executor, or an owner's estate or receiver) are charged to the estate, not personally, unless for mismanagement or bad faith; changes who pays costs after a death.

heading: Amount of costs in an action
review_reason: Fixes Supreme Court costs ($200 before note of issue, $200 after, $300 per trial or inquest); an amount added to a balance or deposit judgment in Supreme Court.

heading: Amount of costs on motion
review_reason: Motion costs are fixed by the court up to $100; a cost either side may owe or recover in a Supreme Court case.

heading: Amount of costs on appeal to appellate division and appellate term
review_reason: Costs on appeals to the Appellate Division and Term; appellate practice.

heading: Amount of costs on appeal to the court of appeals
review_reason: Costs on appeals to the Court of Appeals; appellate practice.

heading: Taxable disbursements
review_reason: Lists the disbursements a party awarded costs taxes in Supreme Court (witness and officer fees, publication, certified copies, docketing, one execution's sheriff fees, deposition transcripts up to $250, searches), and allows disbursements to a party recovering $50 or more without costs.

heading: Additional allowance to plaintiff as of right in real property actions
review_reason: Additional allowances in mortgage foreclosure, partition and real-property claim actions; a lease balance or deposit action is none of these.

heading: Additional allowance in the discretion of the court
review_reason: The court may award up to 5% (max $3,000) in a difficult or extraordinary contested case, and on a motion to enforce a judgment the greater of 5% of the judgment or $50; an amount a landlord may recover for enforcement motions.

heading: Costs upon frivolous claims and counterclaims in actions to recover damages for personal injury, injury to property or wrongful death
review_reason: In an action for injury to property, a frivolous claim, counterclaim or defense brings costs and attorney's fees up to $10,000 against the party or its attorney; applies to a landlord's property-damage claim and a tenant's frivolous defense or counterclaim to it.

heading: Computation by clerk
review_reason: The clerk taxes costs and disbursements on application and strikes any disbursement not shown by affidavit to be necessary and reasonable; this is how the landlord's litigation costs enter a Supreme Court judgment.

heading: Taxation with notice
review_reason: Notice mechanics for taxing costs (five days, itemized bill; none to a defaulting defendant); folded into proposed NY:CPLR-8401-clerk-taxation and changes no amount.

heading: Taxation without notice
review_reason: Taxation without notice and retaxation on five days' notice; folded into proposed NY:CPLR-8401-clerk-taxation and changes no amount.

heading: Judicial review of taxation or retaxation
review_reason: Court review of the clerk's taxation of costs on motion; in-suit mechanics (the taxation rule is proposed at NY:CPLR-8401-clerk-taxation).

heading: Security for costs
review_reason: A defendant may obtain security for costs as of right against a plaintiff that is not a New York resident, domestic corporation or licensed foreign corporation (a former tenant who moved away, an unlicensed foreign owner), and in the court's discretion against executors, receivers and similar plaintiffs.

heading: Stay and dismissal on failure to give security
review_reason: Until ordered security for costs is posted, the plaintiff's action is stayed, and after 30 days it may be dismissed with costs; a deadline that can end a claim.

heading: Undertaking
review_reason: Security for costs is an undertaking of $500 in New York City counties (more if the court fixes it); in NYC Civil Court the minimum is $200 under CCA 1900.

heading: Cancellation of record of judgment discharged in bankruptcy
review_reason: Lets a discharged debtor have a judgment docket marked discharged; the landlord's duty to stop enforcing a discharged balance is stated by US:11USC524(a)(2), and nothing the landlord does turns on the docket entry.

heading: Right of set off against unmatured debts
review_reason: The bankruptcy stay on setoff is stated (US:11USC362(a)(7)-deposit-is-setoff); DCL 151 supplies the state-law setoff right itself, on either side's insolvency event, exercisable against a trustee, receiver or levying creditor.

heading: Notice to creditors of incompetent person or conservatee
review_reason: Where the former tenant's property is managed by a committee (incompetent person) or conservator, the landlord's balance is collected by presenting a verified claim to it by the advertised date; no rule states this incapacity branch.

heading: Authority for committee or conservator to compromise claims
review_reason: A committee or conservator may compromise the former tenant's own claims (the deposit claim) only with court authority; this decides whether a settlement with it binds.

heading: Payment by committee or conservator of claims
review_reason: Consequence of not presenting the claim under DCL 250: the committee's court-directed good-faith payments discharge it and its sureties as to creditors who did not present.

heading: Citation to attend judicial settlement of accounts of committee or conservator
review_reason: Citation to a judicial settlement of a committee's or conservator's accounts; court procedure after the claim is presented under DCL 250.

heading: Service of citation
review_reason: Service of that citation; court procedure.

heading: Proceedings on return of citation
review_reason: Court powers on the citation's return; court procedure.

heading: Permissible exemptions in bankruptcy
review_reason: The refund payee in the tenant's bankruptcy is stated for chapter 7 as the trustee (US:11USC542-refund-payee); DCL 282(i) lets a New York debtor exempt CPLR 5205 property, which includes a residential security deposit, and exempted property leaves the estate, so the remainder is then the debtor's. The rule misses this branch.

heading: Aggregate individual bankruptcy exemption for certain annuities and personal property
review_reason: Caps the aggregate of CPLR 5205(a) personal-property and annuity exemptions; the security deposit is exempt under 5205(g), outside that cap, so the settlement is unchanged.

heading: Exclusivity of exemptions
review_reason: Opts New York debtors out of the federal 522(d) list subject to DCL 285; who is paid follows the exemption the debtor actually claims (proposed at DCL 282), not this section.

heading: Alternative federal exemptions
review_reason: Lets a debtor elect the federal exemption list; the settlement consequence of any exemption of the refund is stated in the rule proposed at DCL 282.

heading: Short title
review_reason: Short title of the EPTL; changes no rule's reach.

heading: References
review_reason: Internal cross-reference convention of the EPTL; changes no rule's reach.

heading: Rules governing use of certain words
review_reason: Singular, plural, gender and 'writing' conventions within the EPTL; no stated rule in the chain depends on them.

heading: Severability
review_reason: Severability clause of the EPTL; changes no rule's reach.

heading: Application
review_reason: Temporal application of the EPTL; transitional.

heading: Codicil
review_reason: Definition of a codicil; the landlord relies on letters, not on testamentary instruments.

heading: Creator
review_reason: Definition of a creator of a disposition; internal to the estate.

heading: Demonstrative disposition
review_reason: Definition of a demonstrative disposition; internal to the estate.

heading: Disposition
review_reason: Definition of a disposition of property; internal to the estate.

heading: Distributee
review_reason: Definition of a distributee; the refund of a deceased tenant is paid to the personal representative, not to distributees (NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee), so the definition changes no payee.

heading: Estate
review_reason: Definition of estate as an interest or aggregate of property; the tenant-death rule does not turn on it.

heading: Fiduciary
review_reason: Broad definition of fiduciary (personal representative, guardian, conservator, trustee); the tenant-death rule pays only a personal representative on letters, which EPTL 1-2.13 defines and which is stated, so the wider list changes no payee.

heading: General disposition
review_reason: Definition of a general disposition; internal to the estate.

heading: Incompetent
review_reason: Definition of incompetent as judicially declared incapable; the stated CPLR incapacity rules use their own identical test.

heading: Infant or minor
review_reason: Definition of infant or minor for the EPTL; capacity of a minor tenant is governed by the CPLR rules already stated (NY:CPLR-1203-1015-5208-parties).

heading: Issue
review_reason: Definition of issue; internal to estate distribution.

heading: Per capita
review_reason: Definition of per capita distribution; internal to estate distribution.

heading: Person
review_reason: Definition of person in the EPTL; no stated rule depends on it.

heading: Personal representative
review_reason: A personal representative is one holding letters, and excludes guardians and conservators; the rule pays the executor or administrator on letters.

heading: Per stirpes
review_reason: Definition of per stirpes distribution among heirs; internal to the estate.

heading: Property
review_reason: Definition of property in the EPTL; no stated rule depends on it (the refund's ownership rests on GOL 7-103 and the tenant-death rule).

heading: Representation
review_reason: Definition of distribution by representation among heirs; internal to the estate.

heading: Specific disposition.
review_reason: Definition of a specific disposition by will; internal to the estate.

heading: Testamentary beneficiary
review_reason: Definition of a testamentary beneficiary; internal to the estate.

heading: Will
review_reason: Definition of a will (electronic wills from 2027-12-12); the landlord relies on letters, not on the will.

heading: Lifetime trust
review_reason: Definition of a lifetime trust, excluding trusts in bank deposits; no stated rule depends on it, and the deposit's trust status comes from GOL 7-103.

heading: Descent and distribution of a decedent's estate
review_reason: Intestate shares among spouse and relatives; the landlord pays the fiduciary, not the heirs (NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee).

heading: Inheritance by non-marital children
review_reason: Inheritance by non-marital children; internal to the estate.

heading: Inheritance by children conceived after the death of an intended
review_reason: Inheritance by posthumously conceived children; internal to the estate, and the landlord pays the fiduciary.

heading: Disqualification of parent to take intestate share
review_reason: Disqualification of a parent from a child's intestate share; internal to the estate.

heading: Other disqualifications
review_reason: A refund owed to a decedent with no heir passes to the State as abandoned property; the unclaimed-refund rules already send it to the Comptroller.

heading: Disqualification of joint tenant in certain instances
review_reason: A joint tenant convicted of murdering the other loses joint bank account funds; not a tenancy matter.

heading: Fiduciaries' powers
review_reason: (b)(5)(A) is the rent-collection power the owner-death rule relies on; (b)(11)-(13) add that a surviving or successor fiduciary may be paid and that any fiduciary may compromise the claim, which the rules do not say.

heading: Tax elections by personal representatives
review_reason: Estate and income tax elections by fiduciaries; internal to the estate.

heading: Power and duty of executor before probate
review_reason: A named executor has no power before letters beyond funeral expenses and preservation; the rule pays the executor only on letters and holds the refund in trust until a fiduciary presents authority.

heading: Validity of execution of power to sell, mortgage or lease real
review_reason: Cures recorded deeds, mortgages or leases executed by fewer than all executors once ten years have passed after recording; not a step in settling a residential tenancy.

heading: Payment of testamentary dispositions or distributive shares
review_reason: When a fiduciary pays legacies and distributive shares; internal to the estate. The creditor's claim period is stated in NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee.

heading: Property held as fiduciary to be kept separate
review_reason: Fiduciaries keep estate property separate; binds the fiduciary. A deposit held by an estate-owned building is already trust money under NY:GOL-7-103(1)-trust.

heading: Limitations on powers and immunities of executors and
review_reason: Voids exoneration clauses for executors and trustees; internal to the estate.

heading: Power of fiduciary or custodian for fiduciary to deposit
review_reason: Bank fiduciaries may hold government securities at a Federal Reserve bank; internal to fiduciary custody of securities, not a tenant's deposit.

heading: Power of Fiduciary or Custodian to Deposit Securities in a
review_reason: Fiduciaries and custodians may hold securities in a clearing corporation; internal to securities custody, not a tenant's deposit.

heading: Power of fiduciary to employ a broker-dealer as custodian
review_reason: A fiduciary may use a broker-dealer as securities custodian; internal to estate administration.

heading: Limited power of fiduciary to amend trust for certain tax
review_reason: A trustee's limited power to amend a trust for tax qualification; internal to trusts.

heading: Principal and income
review_reason: Allocation of receipts between income and principal in trusts and estates; accounting among beneficiaries, not between landlord and tenant.

heading: Power to invest
review_reason: Investment powers of estate and trust fiduciaries; a landlord holding a tenant's deposit is governed by GOL 7-103, not by the fiduciary investment rules.

heading: Prudent investor act
review_reason: Prudent investor rule for trustees; not a tenancy matter.

heading: Judicial control with respect to fiduciary's power to adjust
review_reason: Court review of a trustee's principal-income adjustment; internal to trusts.

heading: Optional unitrust provision
review_reason: Optional unitrust for trusts; not a tenancy matter.

heading: Actions
review_reason: Contract claims survive by and against the personal representative; the rules name the fiduciary as the party who pays and is paid and require substitution.

heading: Action for injury to person or property survives despite death
review_reason: Damage claims survive against the tenant's representative and the estate's claims survive for it; the rules route both through the fiduciary. The punitive bar reaches personal-injury actions only.

heading: Limitations upon recovery where injury causes death
review_reason: Damages when an injury causes death (wrongful death); not a tenancy settlement claim.

heading: Action by representative of representative
review_reason: Decides who may not be paid when the tenant's fiduciary itself dies: the fiduciary's own representative has no authority over the first estate.

heading: How to sue or be sued
review_reason: Suits by or against a personal representative are brought in the representative capacity; a pleading form. That claims run against the fiduciary is stated in NY:ADJ-tenant-death-payee.

heading: When personal and representative causes of action may be joined
review_reason: Joinder of personal and representative claims against a fiduciary; pleading mechanics.

heading: Separate dockets and executions
review_reason: Separate docketing of the personal part of a judgment against a fiduciary; enforcement mechanics with no effect on the lease claim.

heading: Commencement of action against personal representatives
review_reason: Service on one of several co-representatives gives jurisdiction over all; service mechanics.

heading: Want of assets not to be pleaded by personal representative
review_reason: A fiduciary may not plead want of assets against a money claim; recovery is limited at execution (proposed NY:EPTL-11-4.6-execution-leave), so the claim decision does not change.

heading: Leave to issue execution against personal representative
review_reason: The existing rule covers a judgment debtor who dies after judgment; 11-4.6 covers a judgment recovered against the personal representative.

heading: Liability of the personal representative for claims arising out
review_reason: Decides whether a claim arising during estate administration (the estate as owner, or an estate that kept the unit after the tenant died) is pursued against the estate or the fiduciary personally.

heading: Liability of distributees and testamentary beneficiaries
review_reason: Decides whether a deceased tenant's balance may be recovered from heirs and beneficiaries after distribution, and the cap; no rule states it.

heading: Order of liability
review_reason: Fixes whom the landlord pursues first among heirs and beneficiaries and when a prior unpaid claim is a defense.

heading: Extent of liability
review_reason: Caps each heir's liability at its ratable share, which sets what the landlord may finally recover from each.

heading: Action not impaired by failure of creditor or other person to
review_reason: Decides that missing the claim presentation to the fiduciary does not bar suit against heirs, and that the limitation period is not extended.

heading: Action may be joint or several
review_reason: Joinder and impleader among heirs; who is liable and for how much is proposed at EPTL 12-1.1 to 12-1.3.

heading: Effect of application to surrogate to sell real property
review_reason: Stays enforcement against a decedent's real property during an estate accounting; it changes neither liability nor amount of a lease balance.

heading: Effect of judgment
review_reason: Ranks a judgment against an heir ahead of that heir's personal creditors on the inherited property; priority among the heir's creditors changes nothing the landlord does or recovers.

heading: Title of bona fide purchaser from distributee or testamentary
review_reason: Protects good-faith purchasers of inherited property; affects which asset a judgment reaches, not whether or how much the landlord recovers.

heading: Certain assets considered personal property
review_reason: Decides who owns rent accrued before an owner's death and that a deceased tenant's leasehold passes to its personal representative; the owner-death rule does not split accrued from later rent.

heading: Assets
review_reason: A testator's claim against the executor is an estate asset; internal to the estate.

heading: Assets chargeable with payment of estate obligations
review_reason: Which estate assets pay estate debts and the order in which gifts abate; internal administration among beneficiaries. The landlord's claim rank is proposed at SCPA 1811.

heading: Action in supreme court to compromise controversies between
review_reason: Supreme Court action to compromise claims to estate assets under SCPA 2106; internal to the estate.

heading: Rights of payees in non-transferable United States savings
review_reason: Payees of non-transferable U.S. savings bonds take them outside the estate; not a tenancy matter.

heading: Rights of beneficiaries of pension, retirement, death benefit,
review_reason: Designated beneficiaries of pensions, insurance and annuities take outside the will and intestacy rules; those assets are not estate property from which the landlord's claim is paid, which the estate-claim rules already reflect by reaching only estate assets and distributees' receipts.

heading: Designation of trustee to receive proceeds of thrift, savings,
review_reason: Insurance and pension proceeds payable to a designated trustee are not subject to the insured's debts; the landlord's claim against a deceased tenant is paid from estate assets through the fiduciary, and these proceeds are outside the estate, as the stated EPTL 13-3.2 decision already records.

heading: Payment or delivery of property to foreign fiduciaries
review_reason: Adds who may be paid when the tenant was domiciled outside New York at death (a foreign fiduciary) and when that payment discharges.

heading: Action or proceeding by foreign personal or other legal
review_reason: Filing duties when a foreign representative sues in New York; the landlord's payment decision toward a foreign fiduciary is proposed at EPTL 13-3.4.

heading: Disaffirmance of fraudulent acts by personal representative and
review_reason: A fiduciary or a creditor with a claim over $100 against an insolvent estate may set aside fraudulent transfers; an extraordinary creditor remedy that changes no step in presenting or pricing the claim (NY:SCPA-1811-claim-priority).

heading: Purposes of article
review_reason: Title and legislative purposes of the Human Rights Law; the operative housing prohibition is stated by NY:EXEC-296(5)(a)(2)-terms.

heading: Equality of opportunity a civil right
review_reason: Declares equal opportunity in housing a civil right; the operative duties are in section 296, stated by NY:EXEC-296(5)(a)(2)-terms.

heading: Definitions
review_reason: The definitions (housing accommodation, lawful source of income including vouchers paid to the landlord, military status, familial status) give the stated rule its reach, and the rule already applies them to every market-rate unit; the credit definitions are used by the proposed 296-a rule.

heading: Division of human rights
review_reason: Creates the Division of Human Rights; the discrimination rules and remedies that bind the settlement are stated (Exec 296(5), 297(9)).

heading: General policies of division
review_reason: Division of Human Rights policy-making; no party duty.

heading: Statewide campaign for the acceptance, inclusion, tolerance and understanding of diversity
review_reason: Division's diversity awareness campaign; no party duty.

heading: General powers and duties of division
review_reason: Powers and duties of the Division of Human Rights; agency administration.

heading: Unlawful discriminatory practices
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Unlawful discriminatory practices in relation to credit
review_reason: The housing rule covers deductions and whether a balance is pursued; a payment plan on the balance is credit under Exec. Law 292, so 296-a adds its own bar on discriminatory plan decisions and a duty to give reasons on request.

heading: Unlawful discriminatory practices relating to interns
review_reason: Discrimination against unpaid interns by employers; employment, not housing or collection.

heading: Unlawful discriminatory practices relating to non-employees
review_reason: Employer liability for discrimination against contractors in its workplace; employment law, outside the tenancy chain.

heading: Procedure
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Judicial review and enforcement
review_reason: Judicial review of Division of Human Rights orders; procedure after an agency ruling, not a decision in the settlement chain (liability is stated by NY:EXC-297(9)-remedies).

heading: Application of article to certain acts committed outside the state of New York
review_reason: Reaches discrimination committed outside the state against New York residents; settling an NYC unit is conduct within the state, already reached by NY:EXEC-296(5)(a)(2)-terms.

heading: Penal provision
review_reason: Crime of obstructing the Division or wilfully violating its order; changes no settlement step (substantive duties are in 296).

heading: Construction
review_reason: Canon of liberal construction and election of remedies for the complainant; the housing exemptions in NY:EXEC-296(5)(a)(2)-terms are stated as fixed conditions, so their reach does not change.

heading: Separability
review_reason: Severability clause.

heading: Filing of certificates by persons conducting business under assumed name or as partners
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Ownership of merchandise establishments and services to be publicly revealed and displayed
review_reason: A shop or service establishment displays its owner's name on its window or exterior sign; an office-display rule that changes no statement, charge or collection step.

heading: Fictitious copartnership names
review_reason: Misdemeanor to trade under a partner's name or '& Co.' without such a partner; the name a lease or letter uses is governed by the stated GBL 130 and FDCPA true-name rules.

heading: Use of name or address with intent to deceive
review_reason: The federal rule makes a creditor using a third-party-sounding name a debt collector; GBL 133 independently makes a name used with intent to mislead as to identity or connection a misdemeanor, which binds the choice of name on statements and collection letters.

heading: Fraudulent use of the name or title of secret fraternity
review_reason: Fraudulent use of a secret fraternity's name; outside the chain.

heading: Unlawful use of name of benevolent, humane or charitable corporation
review_reason: Use of a charitable corporation's name to gain advantage; outside the chain.

heading: Exhibition or display of the flag
review_reason: 136(c) makes it a misdemeanor to put a representation of the United States or New York flag on business letterhead, envelopes, bill heads or checks, or to use such stationery for business correspondence; the move-out statement, refund check and balance letters are business correspondence. No rule states it.

heading: Unauthorized wearing or use of badge, name or insignia of certain orders and societies
review_reason: Unauthorized wearing of veterans' and fraternal insignia; outside the chain.

heading: Use of certain governmental, military or naval names
review_reason: Sellers of merchandise using 'army', 'government' and similar words in trade names; the chain sells no merchandise, and false government implication in collection is stated at 15 USC 1692e and the city rule importing GBL 601.

heading: Wearing industry badges, or other insignia of identification by unauthorized persons
review_reason: Unauthorized wearing of an employer's registered identification badge; outside the chain.

heading: Unlawful use of the name United Nations
review_reason: Unauthorized use of the United Nations name; outside the chain.

heading: Unlawful possession or use of an identification card issued by United Nations
review_reason: Possession of another person's United Nations identification card; outside the chain.

heading: False identification documents
review_reason: Sale of false identification documents without a NOVELTY mark; outside the chain.

heading: Unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts and practices unlawful
reason: at least one rule-file atom cites this section (provision or source_file)
review_reason: Stated by the rules that cite it (register step 3 citation match); those rules passed independent review rounds 1-5.

heading: Pricing
review_reason: Disclosure of algorithmic pricing when a price is offered to a consumer; move-out charges are not price offers, and lease pricing at leasing is outside the chain.

heading: Residential telephone equipment advertising, sale and warranty requirements
review_reason: Disclosure and warranty rules for sellers of residential telephone equipment; outside the chain.

heading: Voice over internet protocol 911 disclosure
review_reason: 911 limitation disclosures by VoIP sellers; outside the chain.

heading: Additional civil penalty for consumer frauds against elderly persons
review_reason: The rule states the private remedy and that the Attorney General enforces; 349-c adds a supplemental penalty where the deceptive or unfair practice targets a tenant 65 or older.

heading: Energy services company consumers bill of rights
review_reason: ESCO energy contract rules bind energy services companies and their sellers; a landlord's lease utility charge is not an ESCO contract, and submetered and lease utility charges are stated elsewhere.

heading: Counterfeit and non-functional airbags
review_reason: Counterfeit and non-functional airbags; outside the chain.

heading: Pension poaching prevention
review_reason: Veterans' benefits advisers (pension poaching); not a tenancy matter.

heading: Restrictions on applications for and use of credit cards and medical financial products
review_reason: Hospitals and health providers may not fill in patients' medical credit applications; outside the chain.

heading: Observant consumer protection law
review_reason: Labeling of mezuzahs and tefillin; outside the chain.

heading: False advertising unlawful
review_reason: Declares false advertising unlawful; advertising a unit is leasing, outside the settlement chain, and statements and demands are tested under NY:GBL-349-unfair-abusive.

heading: False advertising
review_reason: Definition of false advertising of commodities and employment; not a settlement or collection communication.

heading: Disclosures required in advertisements using the title "doctor"
review_reason: Disclosure when the title 'doctor' is used to sell health goods or services; outside the chain.

heading: Disclosures required in advertisements using a senior specific designation
review_reason: Disclosure of the basis of senior-specific designations in advertising services; outside the chain.

heading: Notice of proposed action
review_reason: Attorney General notice before a false-advertising action; agency procedure.

heading: Civil penalty
review_reason: Sets the civil penalty per violation for practices article 22-A makes unlawful, including GBL 349; the rule states only that the Attorney General enforces.

heading: Construction
review_reason: Private action for false advertising under GBL 350 and 350-a; advertising a unit is leasing, outside the settlement chain.

heading: Exceptions
review_reason: Exempts broadcasters and publishers from the false-advertising article.

heading: After-the-fact referral fees
review_reason: Bars after-the-fact referral fees in real property sales and purchases; sales only, not rentals or settlement.

heading: Short title
review_reason: Short title of the New York Fair Credit Reporting Act; its operative sections are decided where they bind a landlord or collector (GBL 380-b, 380-i, 380-l to 380-o, 380-t).

heading: Definitions
review_reason: Article 25 definitions (consumer report, consumer reporting agency, user); the proposed art. 25 rules use them in their ordinary scope, and none widens or narrows the landlord's or collector's position.

heading: Permissible dissemination of reports
review_reason: Fixes when a NY consumer report on a former tenant may be obtained (locating or collecting the lease balance is a permitted lease use); the (b) application notice is move-in screening and changes nothing at settlement.

heading: Preparation and/or procurement of investigative consumer reports
review_reason: Notice and authorization before an investigative consumer report (character and reputation from interviews); such reports are screening and employment tools, not a step in settling or collecting a tenancy.

heading: Disclosure to consumers
review_reason: Duties of consumer reporting agencies to disclose files to consumers; binds the agency only.

heading: Methods and conditions of disclosure to consumers
review_reason: Methods and charges for an agency's file disclosure; binds the agency only.

heading: Procedure for resolving disputes
review_reason: The agency's reinvestigation of a disputed item; binds the agency. The landlord's duties when a dispute reaches it through an agency are stated by US:15USC1681s-2(b)(1).

heading: Public record information
review_reason: Agency procedures for public-record items; binds the agency only.

heading: Restrictions on investigative consumer reports
review_reason: Limits on reuse of investigative-report information by the agency; binds the agency only.

heading: Requirements on users of consumer reports
review_reason: Subdivision (c) decides whether a landlord may pass a former tenant's consumer report to Handoff, a collector or anyone else at hand-off; (a)-(b) are adverse action on applications and outside the chain.

heading: Prohibited information
review_reason: Lists what a consumer reporting agency may keep or report (including the age limits for collection accounts and judgments); binds the agency, not the landlord or collector that furnishes, whose furnishing duties are stated by US:15USC1681s-2(a)(1)(A) and US:15USC1681b-1681c-report-limits.

heading: Compliance procedures
review_reason: Agency compliance procedures and user certification to the agency; the permitted purposes the user certifies are proposed at GBL 380-B.

heading: Civil liability for willful noncompliance
review_reason: State civil liability (actual, uncapped punitive, fees) for a landlord or collector that willfully misuses a consumer report on a former tenant; no rule states it.

heading: Civil liability for negligent noncompliance
review_reason: State civil liability for a user's negligent noncompliance with article 25; no rule states it.

heading: Jurisdiction of courts
review_reason: Fixes how long a former tenant may sue the landlord or collector for an article 25 violation, which sets the exposure window and record retention.

heading: Obtaining or introducing information under false pretenses
review_reason: Makes it a crime to obtain a former tenant's report under false pretenses or to feed false information to a credit agency to damage the tenant's credit; changes what may be reported.

heading: Unauthorized disclosures by officers or employees
review_reason: Criminal penalty for agency officers or employees who disclose files; binds agency staff only.

heading: Disclosure of medical information
review_reason: Medical information in disclosures goes only to a physician; applies to agency disclosures and adverse-action reasons, not to settling or collecting.

heading: Disclosures to governmental agencies
review_reason: Lets an agency give identifying information to government agencies; binds the agency only.

heading: Theft of identity
review_reason: Prohibits obtaining credit or goods in another person's name with intent to defraud; binds the impostor. A former tenant's claim that someone else incurred the balance is handled under NY:GBL-399-ddd-604-a and the federal and city dispute rules.

heading: Security freeze
review_reason: Decides whether a landlord, its agent or collector may still obtain a former tenant's report after the tenant freezes it: yes, to collect the lease obligation.

heading: Security record freeze for protected minors
review_reason: Security freezes for protected minors placed by credit agencies; binds the agency only.

heading: Severability
review_reason: Severability clause.

heading: Substitution of spurious oils for internal combustion engines
review_reason: Substitution of branded engine lubricating oils; outside the chain.

heading: Optical discs
review_reason: Identification marks on commercially manufactured optical discs; outside the chain.

heading: Anti-phishing act of 2006
review_reason: Bars soliciting identifying information online by impersonating a business without its authority; Handoff or a collector requesting refund bank details in the owner's name acts with the owner's authority, so no settlement step changes.

heading: Cramming prohibited
review_reason: Third-party charges on cable-company telephone bills; not a tenancy matter.

heading: Prohibit persons under eighteen years of age in certain facilities
review_reason: Minors barred from facilities with unclothed performances; outside the chain.

heading: Posting of warnings by commercial entities offering internet access to the public
review_reason: Firewall warning signs where a business offers public internet access; a tenant portal is not public internet access, and data safeguards in the chain are stated (GBL 899-bb).

heading: Information concerning services for human trafficking victims in facilities at truck stops
review_reason: Human-trafficking information in truck-stop restrooms; outside the chain.

heading: Unauthorized installation of certain security devices prohibited
review_reason: Consent and 30-day notice before installing keyless entry in common areas, and no rent increase for it; conduct during the tenancy that fixes no move-out charge or credit.

heading: Skimming awareness notice
review_reason: Skimming notice at points of sale accepting EBT cards; rent and balance payments are not point-of-sale EBT transactions.

heading: Marking retreaded, recapped or recut tires

heading: Number, singular and plural

review_reason: Oath and affidavit include every mode of attestation the law authorizes; every affidavit the chain requires is a court paper, where the affirmation alternative is decided by CPLR 2106 (proposed NY:CPLR-2106-affirmation), so this adds no reach.

heading: Person
review_reason: 'Person' includes a corporation; each stated rule names its actors, and none turns on this default.

heading: Personal injury
review_reason: Personal injury includes libel, slander and malicious prosecution; no deposit or balance claim is a personal-injury claim.

heading: Population
review_reason: Population means the latest federal census count; the chain's population-based rules (the 1,000,000 city carve-outs) apply to NYC on any count.

heading: Quorum and majority
review_reason: Quorum of public boards; outside the chain.

heading: Recital in record of meeting as evidence
review_reason: Recitals in minutes of meetings as evidence; not a settlement matter.

heading: Register of county
review_reason: Acts of a county register satisfy county-clerk requirements; not a settlement matter.

heading: Seal of court, public officer or corporation
review_reason: Form of seals of courts and corporations; seals have no effect on any settlement instrument.

heading: Seal, private

heading: Seal on written instrument
review_reason: A seal on an instrument has no legal effect; no lease, guaranty or release in this chain turns on a seal.

heading: Seal, private as corporate seal
review_reason: Private seals of officers as a corporate seal; seals have no effect on any instrument in this chain.

heading: Signature
review_reason: Several stated rules require a writing 'subscribed' or 'signed' by a party (early termination, guaranty, modification, release); GCN 46 decides what counts as that signature.

heading: State
review_reason: 'State' includes territories and D.C.; the stated capacity rules speak of 'formed outside New York', which this does not change.

review_reason: Present tense includes the future; a construction rule no stated rule turns on.

heading: Time, night
review_reason: Defines night time; no chain act is limited to or barred at night by a rule in scope.

heading: Time, standard
review_reason: Defines the New York standard time that GCN 53 applies to every chain deadline.

heading: Time, use of standard
review_reason: Every chain deadline is kept by New York standard time; this decides whether an electronic statement or refund sent near midnight is on day 14 or day 15.

heading: Trial juror
review_reason: Trial juror means petit juror; outside the chain.

heading: Village
review_reason: Village means an incorporated village; outside NYC and the chain.

heading: Women
review_reason: 'Women' includes girls; no stated rule uses it.

heading: Writing and written
review_reason: 'Writing' includes every legible representation of letters on a material substance; the written-statement and electronic-record rules already fix what counts as a writing in the settlement.

heading: Year, common and leap
review_reason: Which years are leap years; chain deadlines are counted in calendar days under NY:GCN-20, which this does not change.

heading: Year in statute, contract and public or private instrument
review_reason: Month counting is stated (NY:GCN-30); GCN 58 fixes what 'year' means in statutes and leases (twelve months; 365 days with the leap day and the day before counted as one), which governs the chain's yearly periods.

heading: Bastard
review_reason: Terminology for children born out of wedlock; not a settlement matter.

heading: Newspapers
review_reason: What counts as a newspaper for required publication; no settlement notice is published.

heading: Date for determining last completed assessment rolls
review_reason: Assessment rolls for constitutional tax limits; outside the chain.

heading: Size of type
review_reason: The small-print rule is stated (NY:CPLR-4544-small-print); GCN 62 decides how the point size it requires is measured, which decides whether a lease clause may be put in evidence.

heading: Classification of corporations
review_reason: Classification of corporations; the capacity rules turn on domestic or foreign formation, not class.

heading: Definitions
review_reason: Corporate definitions (domestic and foreign corporation, office, business of a corporation); the stated capacity rules use 'formed outside New York' consistently with 66(14), and 66(19) leaves 'doing business' to the governing statute, so no rule's reach changes.

heading: Names of corporation laws
review_reason: Short citations of three corporation laws; changes no rule's reach.

heading: References to repealed provisions
review_reason: A reference to a repealed and re-enacted provision reads as a reference to the new one; no stated rule turns on a renumbered cross-reference.

heading: Titles and head notes
review_reason: Amended section headings carry into tables of contents; changes no rule's reach.

heading: Effect of the repeal of a repealing statute
review_reason: Repealing a repealing statute does not revive the earlier provision; no provision in this chain has been so revived or depends on it.

heading: Effect of the repeal of a statute upon amendments thereof
review_reason: Repeal by the Consolidated Laws includes amending statutes; historical codification with no current settlement effect.

heading: Effect of the repeal of an amending statute
review_reason: Repeal of an amending statute leaves the prior provision in force; no provision in this chain has been so affected.

heading: Effect of repealing statute upon existing rights
review_reason: Decides point-in-time application wherever a rule in the chain is repealed or sunsets (Good Cause 2034-06-15, stabilization 2027-03-31, the pre-2019 and pre-2025 deposit texts): rights and liabilities already accrued survive.

heading: Effect of repealing statute upon pending actions and proceedings
review_reason: Companion to GCN 93 for suits pending when a statute in the chain is repealed or sunsets.

heading: Effect of the repeal of a statute by another statute substantially re-enacting the former
review_reason: A repeal that substantially re-enacts is a continuation; no stated rule turns on it beyond the point-in-time rules already recorded.

heading: Effect of hyphen in schedule of repeals
review_reason: Hyphen in a schedule of repeals includes intermediate numbers; changes no rule's reach.

heading: Application of chapter
